sentences.zh: 文苑四

translations.literal: Literary Grove Four
translations.idiomatic: Literary Grove, Part Four

sentences.zh: ○穆修石延年

translations.literal: ○ Mu Xiu, Shi Yannian
translations.idiomatic: Mu Xiu and Shi Yannian

sentences.zh: 〈（劉潛附）〉

translations.literal: (Liu Qian appended)
translations.idiomatic: (with Liu Qian appended)

sentences.zh: 蕭貫蘇舜欽尹源黃亢黃鑒楊蟠顏太初郭忠恕

translations.literal: Xiao Guan, Su Shunqin, Yin Yuan, Huang Kang, Huang Jian, Yang Pan, Yan Taichu, Guo Zhongshu
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Guan, Su Shunqin, Yin Yuan, Huang Kang, Huang Jian, Yang Pan, Yan Taichu, and Guo Zhongshu

sentences.zh: 穆修，字伯長，鄆州人。

translations.literal: Mu Xiu, style name Bolong, was a man of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Xiu, styled Bolong, was from Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼嗜學，不事章句。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and did not pursue commentarial studies.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he loved learning and did not bother with commentarial pedantry.

sentences.zh: 真宗東封，詔舉齊、魯經行之士，修預選，賜進士出身，調泰州司理參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong made the eastern feng sacrifice, an edict summoned men of classical learning and upright conduct from Qi and Lu; Xiu was among those selected, granted jinshi standing, and appointed judicial aide in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong performed the eastern feng rite, the court called up scholars of classical learning and moral conduct from Qi and Lu. Xiu was chosen, granted jinshi standing, and posted as judicial aide in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 負才，與眾齟齬，通判忌之，使人誣告其罪，貶池州。

translations.literal: Confident in his talent, he clashed with others; the prefectural vice-commissioner resented him and had someone falsely accuse him of crimes, and he was demoted to Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Proud of his talent, he quarreled with those around him. The vice-prefect took offense and had him falsely accused, after which he was banished to Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 中道亡至京師，叩登聞鼓訴冤，不報。

translations.literal: Midway he fled to the capital, struck the Petition Drum to plead his innocence, and received no response.
translations.idiomatic: He fled halfway to the capital, beat the Petition Drum to protest his innocence, and received no answer.

sentences.zh: 居貶所歲餘，遇赦得釋，迎母居京師，間出遊匄以給養。

translations.literal: He lived at his place of exile more than a year; on an amnesty he was released, brought his mother to live in the capital, and from time to time went out begging to support her.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year in exile he was freed by an amnesty, brought his mother to the capital, and would go out from time to time to beg for their keep.

sentences.zh: 久之，補潁州文學參軍，徙蔡州。

translations.literal: After a long while he was appointed literary aide in Yingzhou and transferred to Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he was appointed literary aide in Yingzhou and later transferred to Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 明道中，卒。

translations.literal: In the Mingdao era he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Mingdao reign.

sentences.zh: 修性剛介，好論斥時病，詆誚權貴，人欲與交結，往往拒之。

translations.literal: Xiu's nature was stern and unyielding; he liked to discuss and denounce the ills of the age and to mock the powerful. When people wished to befriend him, he often refused.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was stern and uncompromising, fond of criticizing the ills of the day and ridiculing the powerful. Those who sought his friendship were usually turned away.

sentences.zh: 張知白守亳，亳有豪士作佛廟成，知白使人召修作記，記成，不書士名。

translations.literal: When Zhang Zhibai governed Bo, a local magnate there finished a Buddhist temple; Zhibai sent for Xiu to write its inscription. When it was done, he did not record the man's name.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhang Zhibai was prefect of Bo, a local magnate completed a Buddhist temple there. Zhibai summoned Xiu to compose its inscription, which Xiu finished without naming the patron.

sentences.zh: 士以白金五百遺修為壽，且求載名於記，修投金庭下，俶裝去郡。

translations.literal: The man gave Xiu five hundred taels of silver as a gift and asked that his name appear in the inscription. Xiu threw the silver into the courtyard and packed to leave the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The man sent him five hundred taels of silver as a gift and asked that his name be inscribed. Xiu cast the silver into the courtyard and set out to leave the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 士謝之，終不受，且曰：“吾寧糊口為旅人，終不以匪人汙吾文也。”

translations.literal: The man apologized, but in the end Xiu would not accept it, saying, "I would rather scrape a living as a wanderer than let a base man stain my writing."
translations.idiomatic: The man apologized, but Xiu still refused and said, "I would rather beg my bread as a wanderer than let a scoundrel defile my writing."

sentences.zh: 宰相欲識修，且將用為學官，修終不往見。

translations.literal: The chief minister wished to know Xiu and was about to appoint him a school official, but Xiu never went to see him.
translations.idiomatic: A chief minister wished to meet him and was about to appoint him a school official, but Xiu never went to see him.

sentences.zh: 母死，自負櫬以葬，日誦《孝經》、《喪記》，不飯浮屠為佛事。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he carried the coffin himself to bury her, recited the 《Classic of Filial Piety》 and the 《Mourning Rites》 daily, and would not feed Buddhist monks for funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he bore the coffin himself to the grave, recited the 《Classic of Filial Piety》 and the 《Mourning Rites》 each day, and refused Buddhist funeral services.

sentences.zh: 自五代文敝，國初，柳開始為古文。

translations.literal: From the literary decline of the Five Dynasties, at the founding of the dynasty Liu Kai first revived ancient-style prose.
translations.idiomatic: After the literary decline of the Five Dynasties, Liu Kai at the dynasty's founding was the first to revive ancient-style prose.

sentences.zh: 其後，楊億、劉筠尚聲偶之辭，天下學者靡然從之。

translations.literal: Afterward Yang Yi and Liu Yun prized parallel phrasing and tonal pattern; scholars everywhere followed them in a rush.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yang Yi and Liu Yun championed parallel, ornate phrasing, and scholars everywhere followed suit.

sentences.zh: 修於是時獨以古文稱，蘇舜欽兄弟多從之遊。

translations.literal: At that time Xiu alone was famed for ancient-style prose; Su Shunqin and his brothers often associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: In that era Xiu alone was renowned for ancient-style prose, and Su Shunqin and his brothers often kept his company.

sentences.zh: 修雖窮死，然一時士大夫稱能文者必曰穆參軍。

translations.literal: Though Xiu died in poverty, among the literati of the time anyone praised for writing was called Military Aide Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Though he died in poverty, whenever men of letters of the day spoke of fine writing they meant Military Aide Mu.

sentences.zh: 慶曆中，祖無擇訪得所著詩、書、序、記、誌等數十首，集為三卷。

translations.literal: In the Qingli era Zu Wuzhe sought out his poems, letters, prefaces, records, epitaphs, and the like—several dozen pieces—and collected them in three fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingli reign Zu Wuzhe gathered several dozen of his poems, letters, prefaces, records, and epitaphs into three fascicles.

sentences.zh: 石延年，字曼卿，先世幽州人。

translations.literal: Shi Yannian, style name Manqing, was by ancestry from Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yannian, styled Manqing, came of a Youzhou family.

sentences.zh: 晉以幽州遺契丹，其祖舉族南走，家於宋城。

translations.literal: When Jin ceded Youzhou to the Khitan, his grandfather led the whole clan south and settled at Songcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin dynasty yielded Youzhou to the Khitan, his grandfather led the entire clan south and made their home at Songcheng.

sentences.zh: 延年為人跌宕任氣節，讀書通大略，為文勁健，於詩最工而善書。

translations.literal: Yannian was unrestrained and bold in spirit; in reading he grasped the broad outlines. His prose was forceful, his poetry his finest art, and he was skilled at calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: Yannian was free-spirited and high-minded. He read for the large design rather than detail, wrote vigorous prose, excelled most in poetry, and was accomplished at calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 累舉進士不中，真宗錄三舉進士，以為三班奉職，延年恥不就。

translations.literal: He repeatedly failed the jinshi examination. Emperor Zhenzong enrolled those who had presented three times and made them Third-Rank Attendants; Yannian was ashamed and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He failed the jinshi examination repeatedly. Emperor Zhenzong enrolled candidates who had presented three times and appointed them Third-Rank Attendants, but Yannian was too proud to take the post.

sentences.zh: 張知白素奇之，謂曰：“母老乃擇祿耶？”

translations.literal: Zhang Zhibai had long admired him and said, "Your mother is old—will you now choose an official salary?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhibai, who had long admired him, said, "Your mother is old—will you choose an official salary only now?"

sentences.zh: 延年不得已就命。

translations.literal: Yannian had no choice but to accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: At last Yannian had no choice but to accept.

sentences.zh: 後以右班殿直改太常寺太祝，知金鄉縣，有治名。

translations.literal: Later, from Right-Ban Palace Guard he was changed to Grand Sacrificer in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and governed Jinxiang County, where he gained a reputation for good administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred from Right-Ban Palace Guard to Grand Sacrificer in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and appointed magistrate of Jinxiang, where he earned a name for effective rule.

sentences.zh: 用薦者通判乾寧軍，徙永靜軍，為大理評事、館閣校勘，曆光祿、大理寺丞，上書章獻太后，請還政天子。

translations.literal: On recommendation he became vice-commissioner of Qianning Army, then moved to Yongjing Army; he served as reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review, collator in the Hall of Literature, and passed through posts in the Court of Imperial Entertainments and as vice-director of the Court of Judicial Review, and memorialized Empress Dowager Zhangxian to return rule to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for office, he served as vice-commissioner of Qianning and then Yongjing armies, and held posts as judicial reviewer, Hall collator, and offices in the Courts of Imperial Entertainments and Judicial Review. He memorialized Empress Dowager Zhangxian to restore rule to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 太后崩，範諷欲引延年，延年力止之。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager died, Fan Feng wished to bring Yannian forward; Yannian strongly stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: After the empress dowager's death Fan Feng wanted to advance Yannian, but Yannian firmly dissuaded him.

sentences.zh: 後諷敗，延年坐與諷善，落職通判海州。

translations.literal: Later Feng fell, and Yannian was implicated for friendship with Feng, demoted to vice-commissioner of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng later fell from power, Yannian was punished for their friendship and demoted to vice-commissioner of Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，為秘閣校理，遷太子中允，同判登聞鼓院。

translations.literal: After a long while he became collator of the Secret Archive, was promoted to Palace Companion, and served jointly as judge of the Petition Drum Court.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he was made collator of the Secret Archive, promoted to Palace Companion, and appointed associate judge of the Petition Drum Court.

sentences.zh: 嚐上言天下不識戰三十餘年，請為二邊之備。

translations.literal: He once memorialized that the realm had not known war for more than thirty years and asked that the two frontiers be prepared.
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted a memorial saying the empire had not known war for more than thirty years and urging preparations on both frontiers.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not reply.

sentences.zh: 及元昊反，始思其言，召見，稍用其說。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao rebelled, they first recalled his words, summoned him, and gradually adopted his proposals.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao rebelled, the court recalled his advice, summoned him, and gradually put his ideas to use.

sentences.zh: 命往河東籍鄉兵，凡得十數萬，時邊將遂欲以扞賊，延年笑曰：“此得吾粗也。

translations.literal: He was ordered to go to Hedong to register militia and gathered well over a hundred thousand. The frontier generals then wished to use them to repel the enemy. Yannian laughed and said, "This only gets at my rough idea.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to Hedong to register local militia, he mustered well over a hundred thousand men. Frontier commanders then wanted to use them against the enemy. Yannian laughed and said, "That only scratches the surface of what I mean.

sentences.zh: 夫不教之兵勇怯相雜，若怯者見敵而動，則勇者亦牽而潰矣。

translations.literal: Untrained troops mix the brave with the timid; if the timid stir at sight of the enemy, the brave are dragged into flight as well.
translations.idiomatic: Untrained soldiers mingle courage with cowardice; if the cowards move at sight of the enemy, the brave are dragged into rout as well.

sentences.zh: 今既不暇教，宜募其敢行者，則人人皆勝兵也。”

translations.literal: Now that there is no time to train them, one should recruit those who dare act—then every man would be a victorious soldier."
translations.idiomatic: Since there is no time to train them now, recruit those who dare to fight, and every man will be elite troops."

sentences.zh: 又嚐請募人使唃廝囉及回鶻舉兵攻元昊，帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: He also once asked to recruit men to induce Gusiluo and the Uyghurs to raise troops against Yuan Hao, and the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed recruiting agents to induce Gusiluo and the Uyghurs to attack Yuan Hao, which the emperor welcomed.

sentences.zh: 延年喜劇飲，嚐與劉潛造王氏酒樓對飲，終日不交一言。

translations.literal: Yannian loved heavy drinking. Once he and Liu Qian went to the Wang family's wine tower and drank facing each other all day without exchanging a word.
translations.idiomatic: Yannian loved to drink heavily. Once he and Liu Qian went to the Wang family's tavern and drank facing each other all day without saying a word.

sentences.zh: 王氏怪其飲多，以為非常人，益奉美酒肴果，二人飲啖自若，至夕無酒色，相揖而去。

translations.literal: The Wangs marveled at how much they drank, took them for extraordinary men, and offered still finer wine, dishes, and fruit. The two ate and drank as before; by evening they showed no sign of drink, bowed to each other, and left.
translations.idiomatic: The Wangs were astonished by how much they drank and took them for extraordinary men, bringing still finer wine, food, and fruit. The two drank and ate as calmly as before, showed no sign of intoxication by evening, bowed to each other, and departed.

sentences.zh: 明日，都下傳王氏酒樓有二仙來飲，已乃知劉、石也。

translations.literal: The next day the capital spread word that two immortals had come to drink at the Wang wine tower; only later did people learn it was Liu and Shi.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the capital buzzed that two immortals had drunk at the Wang tavern; only later did people learn it was Liu and Shi.

sentences.zh: 延年雖酣放，若不可攖以世務，然與人論天下事，是非無不當。

translations.literal: Though Yannian was wild in drink and seemed untouchable by worldly affairs, when he discussed the realm with others his judgments of right and wrong were never off.
translations.idiomatic: Though he drank freely and seemed beyond the reach of worldly business, in discussion of public affairs his judgments were never wrong.

sentences.zh: 初，與天章閣待制吳遵路同使河東，及卒，遵路言於朝廷，特官其一子。

translations.literal: Earlier he had served in Hedong together with Wu Zunlu, Hanlin academician at the Tianzhang Pavilion. When Yannian died, Zunlu spoke to the court and a special office was granted to one of his sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier served in Hedong with Wu Zunlu, academician at the Tianzhang Pavilion. After Yannian's death Zunlu spoke to the court, and one of his sons received a special appointment.

sentences.zh: 劉潛字仲方，曹州定陶人。

translations.literal: Liu Qian, style name Zhongfang, was a man of Dingtao in Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qian, styled Zhongfang, was from Dingtao in Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 少卓逸有大誌，好為古文，以進士起家，為淄州軍事推官。

translations.literal: In youth he was outstanding and high-minded with great ambition, loved ancient-style prose, entered office through the jinshi degree, and became military judicial aide in Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was exceptional and ambitious, devoted to ancient-style prose, entered service as a jinshi, and became military judicial aide in Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 嚐知蓬萊縣，代還，過鄆州，方與曼卿飲，聞母暴疾，亟歸。

translations.literal: He once governed Penglai County; on returning from his replacement term he passed through Yanzhou and was just drinking with Manqing when he heard his mother had taken sudden illness and hurried home.
translations.idiomatic: He once served as magistrate of Penglai. On his return from a replacement tour he passed through Yanzhou and was drinking with Manqing when he heard his mother had fallen suddenly ill and rushed home.

sentences.zh: 母死，潛一慟遂絕，其妻復撫潛大號而死。

translations.literal: When his mother died, Qian gave one great cry and expired; his wife then embraced him, wailed loudly, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, Qian gave one great cry and died. His wife then embraced him, wailed, and died as well.

sentences.zh: 時人傷之，曰：“子死於孝，妻死於義。”

translations.literal: People of the time mourned them, saying, "The son died in filial piety; the wife died in righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: People mourned them, saying, "The son died for filial piety; the wife died for righteousness."

sentences.zh: 同時以文學稱京東者，齊州曆城有李冠，舉進士不第，得同《三禮》出身，調乾寧主簿，卒。

translations.literal: At the same time, among those famed in Jingdong for letters was Li Guan of Licheng in Qizhou. He failed the jinshi examination, gained office through the 《Three Rites》 examination, was appointed recorder at Qianning, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Among those famed in Jingdong for literary talent at the time was Li Guan of Licheng in Qizhou. He failed the jinshi examination, entered office through the 《Three Rites》 examination, was posted as recorder at Qianning, and died.

sentences.zh: 有《東皋集》二十卷。

translations.literal: He left the 《Eastern Mound Collection》 in twenty fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: He left a twenty-fascicle collection called the 《Eastern Mound Collection》.

sentences.zh: 蕭貫，字貫之，臨江軍新喻人。

translations.literal: Xiao Guan, courtesy name Guanzhi, was a native of Xinyu in Linjiang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Guan, courtesy name Guanzhi, was from Xinyu in Linjiang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 俊邁能文，尚氣概。

translations.literal: Bold and able in letters, he valued spirit and mettle.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and gifted in letters, he prized spirit and mettle.

sentences.zh: 舉進士甲科，爲大理評事，通判安、宿二州，遷太子中允、直史館。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the first rank, was made case reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review, served as vice prefect of An and Su prefectures, and was promoted to palace attendant and compiler in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the first rank, served as case reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and vice prefect of An and Su, and was promoted to palace attendant and compiler in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，進太常丞、同判禮院。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong acceded, he was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and associate administrator of the Rites Institute.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong acceded, he rose to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and associate administrator of the Rites Institute.

sentences.zh: 歷吏部南曹、開封府推官、三司鹽鐵判官，爲京東轉運使。

translations.literal: He served in the southern bureau of the Ministry of Personnel, as investigating officer in Kaifeng Prefecture, and as salt and iron commissioner in the Three Departments, then became transport commissioner of Jingdong.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Ministry of Personnel's southern bureau, as investigating officer in Kaifeng Prefecture, and as salt and iron commissioner in the Three Departments, then became transport commissioner of Jingdong.

sentences.zh: 時提舉捉賊劉舜卿善捕盜，號“劉鐵彈”，恃功為不法，前後畏其凶悍，莫敢治。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Shunqing, commissioner for apprehending bandits, was skilled at catching thieves and was called Iron Bullet Liu. He relied on his achievements to act lawlessly; those before and after feared his ferocity and none dared punish him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Liu Shunqing, commissioner for apprehending bandits, was skilled at catching thieves and known as Iron Bullet Liu. He used his exploits to break the law, and for years no one dared punish him because of his ferocity.

sentences.zh: 貫至，發之，廢為民。

translations.literal: When Guan arrived, he exposed him and reduced him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan arrived he exposed the case and stripped Liu of office, reducing him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 徙江東，改知洪州，累遷尚書刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Jiangdong, then appointed prefect of Hongzhou, and was promoted repeatedly to vice director in the Ministry of Justice in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Jiangdong, he was later appointed prefect of Hongzhou and rose to vice director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 坐前使江東不察所部吏受賕，降知饒州。

translations.literal: Because on his earlier mission to Jiangdong he had not detected bribery among subordinate officials, he was demoted to prefect of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to prefect of Raozhou for failing, on an earlier tour in Jiangdong, to detect bribery among his subordinates.

sentences.zh: 有撫州司法參軍孫齊者，初以明法得官，以其妻杜氏留裏中，而紿娶周氏入蜀。

translations.literal: There was Sun Qi, judicial aide in Fuzhou, who first gained office through the statutes examination, left his wife Lady Du in the village, and deceptively married Lady Zhou and went into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: There was a judicial aide in Fuzhou named Sun Qi who had first gained office through the statutes examination. He left his wife Lady Du at home, deceived Lady Zhou into marriage, and went into Shu.

sentences.zh: 後周欲訴於官，齊斷發誓出杜氏。

translations.literal: Later Zhou wished to bring suit in court; Qi cut his hair and swore an oath to send Lady Du away.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou later tried to sue, Qi cut his hair and swore to send Lady Du away.

sentences.zh: 久之，又納倡陳氏，挈周所生子之撫州。

translations.literal: After a long while he took the courtesan Lady Chen and brought Zhou's son to Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he took a courtesan named Chen and brought Zhou's son with him to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 未逾月，周氏至，齊捽置廡下，出偽券曰：“若傭婢也，敢爾邪！”

translations.literal: Within a month Zhou arrived. Qi seized her and threw her under the eaves, produced a forged contract, and said, "You are a hired servant—how dare you!"
translations.idiomatic: Within a month Zhou arrived. Qi seized her, threw her under the eaves, produced a forged contract, and said, "You are a hired servant—how dare you behave this way!"

sentences.zh: 乃殺其所生子。

translations.literal: He then killed the son she had borne.
translations.idiomatic: Then he killed the son she had borne.

sentences.zh: 周訴於州及轉運使，皆不受。

translations.literal: Zhou appealed to the prefecture and the transport commissioner; neither would accept the case.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou appealed to the prefecture and the transport commissioner, but neither would hear her case.

sentences.zh: 人或告之曰：“得知饒州蕭史君者訴之，事當白矣。”

translations.literal: Someone told her, "If you appeal to Recorder Xiao of Raozhou, the matter will be brought to light."
translations.idiomatic: Someone told her, "If you appeal to Recorder Xiao in Raozhou, the matter will be cleared up."

sentences.zh: 周氏以布衣書姓名，乞食道上，馳告貫。

translations.literal: Lady Zhou, in plain clothes with her name written on them, begged food along the road and hurried to tell Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Wearing plain clothes with her name written on them, Zhou begged along the road and rushed to tell Guan.

sentences.zh: 撫非所部，而貫特為治之。

translations.literal: Fuzhou was not in his jurisdiction, yet Guan specially took up the case.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhou was outside his jurisdiction, yet Guan took up the case anyway.

sentences.zh: 更赦，猶編管齊、濠州。

translations.literal: Despite an amnesty, Qi was still registered and confined in Qi and Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Despite an amnesty, Qi was still registered and exiled to Qi and Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部員外郎，召還，將試知制誥，會營建獻、懿二皇太后陵，未及試而卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director in the Ministry of War, recalled to court, and was about to be tested for drafting imperial edicts when construction of the tombs of the Xian and Yi empress dowagers intervened; before the test he died.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice director in the Ministry of War and recalled to court, he was about to be examined for drafting imperial edicts when work began on the tombs of the Xian and Yi empress dowagers; he died before the examination could take place.

sentences.zh: 貫臨事敢為，不苟合於時。

translations.literal: Guan was bold in handling affairs and would not trim his conduct to the times.
translations.idiomatic: In office Guan acted boldly and would not trim his conduct to suit the times.

sentences.zh: 初，感疾，夢綠衣中人召至帝所，賦《禁中曉寒歌》，詞語清麗，人以比唐李賀。

translations.literal: Early on, when he fell ill, he dreamed that a man in green robes summoned him to the emperor's presence, where he composed the 《Dawn Cold in the Palace Song》; the language was refined and clear, and people compared him to Li He of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: When he first fell ill he dreamed that a man in green robes summoned him before the emperor, where he composed the 《Dawn Cold in the Palace Song》. The language was refined, and people compared him to the Tang poet Li He.

sentences.zh: 蘇舜欽，字子美，參知政事易簡之孫。

translations.literal: Su Shunqin, style name Zimei, was grandson of the Vice Grand Councilor Yi Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shunqin, styled Zimei, was a grandson of Vice Grand Councilor Yi Jian.

sentences.zh: 父耆，有才名，嚐為工部郎中、直集賢院。

translations.literal: His father Qi was famed for talent and once served as director in the Ministry of Works and academician in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qi was a man of literary reputation who had served as director in the Ministry of Works and academician in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 舜欽少慷慨有大誌，狀貌怪偉。

translations.literal: Shunqin in youth was high-spirited with great ambition; his appearance was strange and imposing.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Shunqin was ardent and ambitious, with a strange and imposing appearance.

sentences.zh: 當天聖中，學者為文多病偶對，獨舜欽與河南穆修好為古文、歌詩，一時豪俊多從之遊。

translations.literal: During the Tiansheng era scholars' writing mostly suffered from parallel ornament; only Shunqin and Mu Xiu of Henan delighted in ancient-style prose and songs, and many leading men of the time associated with them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiansheng era most scholars wrote in ornate parallel style. Only Shunqin and Mu Xiu of Henan devoted themselves to ancient-style prose and poetry, and many leading men of the day sought their company.

sentences.zh: 初以父任補太廟齋郎，調滎陽縣尉。

translations.literal: At first, through his father's privilege, he was appointed Temple Aide and was transferred to assistant magistrate of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered office through his father's privilege as Temple Aide and was posted as assistant magistrate of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 玉清昭應宮災，舜欽年二十一，詣登聞鼓院上疏曰：

translations.literal: When the Yuqing Zhaoying Palace burned, Shunqin was twenty-one and went to the Petition Drum Court to submit a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuqing Zhaoying Palace burned, Shunqin was twenty-one. He went to the Petition Drum Court and submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 烈士不避鈇鉞而進諫，明君不諱過失而納忠，是以懷策者必吐上前，蓄冤者無至腹誹。

translations.literal: Men of resolve do not shun axe and halberd to offer remonstrance; enlightened rulers do not conceal faults but accept loyal counsel. Thus those who hold plans are sure to speak before the throne, and those who harbor grievances need not keep slander in their bellies.
translations.idiomatic: Men of resolve do not shrink from axe and halberd when they remonstrate; enlightened rulers do not hide their faults but accept loyal counsel. Those with plans speak frankly before the throne, and those with grievances need not mutter in secret.

sentences.zh: 然言之難不如容之難，容之難不如行之難，有言之必容之行之，則三代之主也，幸陛下留聽焉。

translations.literal: Yet to speak is not so hard as to accept, and to accept is not so hard as to act. A ruler who accepts what is spoken and acts upon it is a lord of the Three Dynasties. I beg Your Majesty to hear me out.
translations.idiomatic: Yet speaking is easier than accepting, and accepting is easier than acting. A ruler who hears, accepts, and acts is a lord of the Three Dynasties. I beg Your Majesty to hear me through.

sentences.zh: 臣觀今歲自春徂夏，霖雨陰晦，未嚐少止，農田被菑者幾於十九。

translations.literal: Your servant observes that from spring through summer this year continuous rain and gloom have scarcely let up, and farmland afflicted by disaster amounts to nearly nine-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant observes that from spring through summer this year rain and gloom have scarcely ceased, and nearly nine-tenths of the farmland has been ruined.

sentences.zh: 臣以謂任用失人、政令多過、賞罰弗中之所召也。

translations.literal: Your servant believes this was summoned by wrongful appointments, excessive policies, and rewards and punishments that missed the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant believes this has been summoned by wrongful appointments, excessive policies, and misplaced rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 天之降災，欲悟陛下，而大臣歸咎於刑獄之濫，陛下聽之，故肆赦天下以為禳救。

translations.literal: Heaven sent disaster to awaken Your Majesty, but great ministers blamed excessive punishments. Your Majesty listened and therefore proclaimed a general amnesty as a rite of expiation.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sent disaster to awaken Your Majesty, but great ministers blamed excessive punishments. Your Majesty accepted this and proclaimed a general amnesty as expiation.

sentences.zh: 如此則是殺人者不死，傷人者不抵罪，而欲以合天意也。

translations.literal: In this way murderers would not die and those who wounded others would not pay for their crimes, yet the court wished thereby to accord with Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: In this way murderers would go unpunished and assailants would escape penalty, yet the court hoped thereby to satisfy Heaven.

sentences.zh: 古者斷決滯訟以平水旱，不聞用赦，故赦下之後，陰霾及今。

translations.literal: In antiquity they resolved stale lawsuits to quell flood and drought; one does not hear of using amnesty. Thus after the amnesty was issued, gloom has continued to the present.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity stale lawsuits were resolved to quell flood and drought; amnesty was not the remedy. Yet after the amnesty was issued, gloom has continued to this day.

sentences.zh: 前誌曰：“積陰生陽，陽生則火災見焉。”

translations.literal: Earlier records say, "When yin accumulates it generates yang; when yang arises, fire disaster appears."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier records say, "When yin accumulates it gives rise to yang; when yang arises, fire disaster appears."

sentences.zh: 乘夏之氣發泄於玉清宮，震雨雜下，烈焰四起，樓觀萬疊，數刻而盡，非慢於火備，乃天之垂戒也。

translations.literal: Released in summer's qi at the Yuqing Palace, thunder and rain fell together, flames leapt on every side, and tier upon tier of towers and halls were consumed in moments. This was not neglect of fire precautions but Heaven's warning.
translations.idiomatic: Released in the qi of summer at the Yuqing Palace, thunder and rain fell together and flames leapt on every side until tier upon tier of towers and halls were consumed in moments. This was not neglect of fire precautions but Heaven's warning.

sentences.zh: 陛下當降服、減膳、避正寢，責躬罪己，下哀痛之詔，罷非業之作，拯失職之民，察輔弼及左右無裨國體者罷之，竊弄權威者去之；

translations.literal: Your Majesty should lower your garments, reduce your meals, and avoid the main palace; blame yourself and confess fault; issue a mournful edict; halt unessential works; rescue the people who have lost their livelihood; examine aides and attendants who do not benefit the state and remove them, and dismiss those who usurp authority in secret;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should lower your garments, reduce your meals, and avoid the main palace; blame yourself and confess your faults; issue a mournful edict; halt unessential works; rescue the destitute; examine aides and attendants who do not serve the state and remove them, and dismiss those who secretly abuse authority;

sentences.zh: 念政刑之失，收芻蕘之論，庶幾所以變災為祐。

translations.literal: reflect on failures in government and punishment, gather the talk of grass and firewood sellers—then perhaps disaster may be turned to blessing.
translations.idiomatic: reflect on failures in government and law, gather counsel even from common folk, and perhaps disaster may be turned to blessing.

sentences.zh: 浹日之間，未聞為此，而將計工役以圖修復，都下之人聞者駭惑，聚首橫議，鹹謂非宜。

translations.literal: Within a few days one heard nothing of this, but instead plans for labor to rebuild. Those in the capital who heard were alarmed and bewildered; they gathered and argued openly, all saying it was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Within days one heard nothing of this, but only plans for labor to rebuild. People in the capital were alarmed; they gathered and argued openly, all saying it was wrong.

sentences.zh: 皆曰章聖皇帝勤儉十餘年，天上富庶，帑府流衍，乃作斯宮，及其畢功，海內虛竭。

translations.literal: All said that for more than ten years Emperor Zhangsheng had been frugal and diligent, the realm above was rich, and the treasury overflowed—yet he built this palace, and when it was finished the empire within the seas was drained empty.
translations.idiomatic: All said that for more than ten years Emperor Zhangsheng had been frugal and diligent while the realm grew rich and the treasury overflowed, yet he built this palace, and when it was finished the empire was drained.

sentences.zh: 陛下即位及十年，數遭水旱，雖征賦鹹入，而百姓困乏。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has been on the throne nearly ten years and has suffered repeated flood and drought; though taxes are fully collected, the common people are exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has reigned nearly ten years and has suffered repeated floods and droughts. Though taxes are fully collected, the people are exhausted.

sentences.zh: 若大興土木，則費知紀極，財力耗於內，百姓勞於下，內耗下勞，何以為國！

translations.literal: If great construction is launched, expense will know no limit; wealth and strength will be consumed within and the people wearied below. With inner drain and lower exhaustion, how can there be a state!
translations.idiomatic: If great construction is launched, expense will know no limit, the treasury will be drained within and the people wearied below. With the state exhausted above and the people exhausted below, how can the realm endure!

sentences.zh: 況天災之，己違之，是欲競天，無省己之意。

translations.literal: Moreover Heaven has sent disaster, yet the court has already defied it—this is to contend with Heaven and shows no intent to examine oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Heaven has sent disaster, yet the court has already defied it. This is to contend with Heaven and shows no intent of self-examination.

sentences.zh: 逆天不祥，安己難任，欲祈厚貺，其可得乎！

translations.literal: To defy Heaven is inauspicious; to comfort oneself is hard to sustain. If one wishes to pray for great blessing, how can it be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: To defy Heaven is inauspicious; to comfort oneself alone cannot last. How can one pray for great blessing and expect to receive it!

sentences.zh: 今為陛下計，莫若求吉士，去佞人，修德以勤至治，使百姓足給而征稅寬減，則可以謝天意而安民情矣。

translations.literal: What Your servant now counsels is that Your Majesty seek worthy men, remove flatterers, cultivate virtue and strive for perfect rule, so that the people have enough and taxes are eased—then one may answer Heaven's intent and settle the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: What your servant counsels now is that Your Majesty seek worthy men, remove flatterers, cultivate virtue and strive for perfect rule, so that the people have enough and taxes are eased. Then you may answer Heaven and settle the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 夫賢君見變，修道除凶，亂世無象，天不譴告。

translations.literal: Worthy rulers, seeing change, cultivate the Way and remove misfortune; in chaotic ages there are no omens, and Heaven does not warn.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy rulers, seeing change, cultivate the Way and remove misfortune. In chaotic ages there are no omens, and Heaven does not warn.

sentences.zh: 今幸天見之變，是陛下修己之日，豈可忽哉！

translations.literal: Now we are fortunate that Heaven has shown change—this is the day for Your Majesty to cultivate yourself. How can it be neglected!
translations.idiomatic: Now Heaven has shown change—this is the day for Your Majesty to cultivate yourself. How can it be neglected!

sentences.zh: 昔漢元帝三年，茂陵白鶴館災，詔曰：“ 乃者火災降於孝武園館，朕戰慄恐懼，不燭變異，罪在朕躬。

translations.literal: In the past, in the third year of Emperor Yuan of Han, the White Crane Hall at Maoling burned. An edict said, "Recently fire descended on Emperor Wu's park hall. We tremble in fear, having not illumined these changes—the fault lies in Our person.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Emperor Yuan of Han the White Crane Hall at Maoling burned. The edict said, "Recently fire descended on Emperor Wu's park hall. We tremble in fear, having failed to understand these changes—the fault lies in Us alone.

sentences.zh: 群有司又不肯極言朕過，以至於斯，將何寤焉！”

translations.literal: The host of officials again would not speak fully of Our faults, until it came to this—how shall We awaken!"
translations.idiomatic: The host of officials again would not speak fully of Our faults, until it came to this. How shall We awaken!"

sentences.zh: 夫茂陵不及上都，白鶴館大不及此宮，彼尚降詔四方，以求己過，是知帝王憂危念治，汲汲如此。

translations.literal: Yet Maoling was not as important as the upper capital, and the White Crane Hall was far smaller than this palace—still they issued edicts to the four quarters to seek their own faults. This shows how urgently emperors, anxious for peril and mindful of order, act thus.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Maoling was less important than the upper capital, and the White Crane Hall far smaller than this palace—still they issued edicts throughout the realm to seek their own faults. This shows how urgently rulers anxious for peril and mindful of order act.

sentences.zh: 臣又按《五行志》：賢佞分別，官人有敘，率由舊章，禮重功勳，則火得其性。

translations.literal: Your servant further consults the 《Treatise on the Five Phases》: when worthy and flatterer are distinguished, officials have proper order, all follow old statutes, and ritual honors merit, then fire keeps its proper nature.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant further consults the 《Treatise on the Five Phases》: when worthy men are distinguished from flatterers, officials keep their proper order, old statutes are followed, and ritual honors merit, fire keeps its proper nature.

sentences.zh: 若信道不篤，或耀虛偽，讒夫昌，邪勝正，則火失其性，自上而降。

translations.literal: If faith in the Way is not firm, or empty show is displayed, slanderers flourish and evil overcomes right, then fire loses its nature and descends from above.
translations.idiomatic: If faith in the Way is not firm, if empty show is displayed, if slanderers flourish and evil overcomes right, fire loses its nature and descends from above.

sentences.zh: 及濫炎妄起，燔宗廟，燒宮室，雖興師徒而不能救。

translations.literal: When rampant flames rise wantonly, burning ancestral temples and palace halls, even raising armies and labor cannot save them.
translations.idiomatic: When rampant flames rise wantonly and burn ancestral temples and palace halls, even armies and labor gangs cannot save them.

sentences.zh: 魯成公三年，新宮災，劉向謂成公信三桓子孫之讒、逐父臣之應。

translations.literal: In the third year of Duke Cheng of Lu the new palace burned; Liu Xiang said it responded to Cheng's belief in the Three Huan descendants' slander and his expulsion of his father's ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Duke Cheng of Lu the new palace burned. Liu Xiang said it responded to Cheng's belief in the Three Huan's slanders and his expulsion of his father's ministers.

sentences.zh: 襄公九年春，宋火，劉向謂宋公聽讒、逐其大夫華弱奔魯之應。

translations.literal: In spring of the ninth year of Duke Xiang, Song caught fire; Liu Xiang said it responded to Duke Mu of Song listening to slander and driving out his minister Hua Ruo, who fled to Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the ninth year of Duke Xiang, Song caught fire. Liu Xiang said it responded to Duke Mu listening to slander and driving out his minister Hua Ruo, who fled to Lu.

sentences.zh: 今宮災豈亦有是乎？

translations.literal: Does today's palace fire perhaps have such a cause as well?
translations.idiomatic: Might today's palace fire have a similar cause?

sentences.zh: 願陛下拱默內省而追革之，罷再造之勞，述前世之法，天下之幸也。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to sit in silent reflection, examine yourself inwardly and reform, halt the labor of rebuilding, and follow the methods of former ages—then the realm will be fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to reflect in silence, examine yourself and reform, halt rebuilding, and follow the methods of former ages. That would be the fortune of the realm.

sentences.zh: 又上書曰：

translations.literal: He submitted another memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 曆觀前代聖神之君，好聞讜議，蓋以四海至遠，民有隱慝，不可以遍照，故無間愚賤之言而擇用之。

translations.literal: Reviewing the sage and divine rulers of former ages, they loved to hear straight counsel, for the realm within the four seas is vast and the people have hidden resentments that cannot all be illumined. Thus they did not disdain the words of the foolish and lowly but chose and used them.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing the sage rulers of former ages, they loved to hear frank counsel. The realm is vast and the people harbor hidden grievances that cannot all be seen. Thus they did not disdain the words of the lowly but chose and used them.

sentences.zh: 然後朝無遺政，物無遁情，雖有佞臣，邪謀莫得而進也。

translations.literal: Then the court had no neglected policies and nothing escaped notice; though there were flatterers, wicked schemes could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Then the court left no policy neglected and nothing escaped notice; though flatterers remained, wicked schemes could not advance.

sentences.zh: 臣睹乙亥詔書，戒越職言事，播告四方，無不驚惑，往往竊議，恐非出陛下之意。

translations.literal: Your servant has seen the yihai edict warning against speaking out of office and broadcasting it to the four quarters. All were alarmed and bewildered and often whispered in private, fearing it did not come from Your Majesty's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has seen the yihai edict warning against speaking outside one's office and broadcasting it throughout the realm. Everyone was alarmed and whispered in private, fearing it did not reflect Your Majesty's intent.

sentences.zh: 蓋陛下即位以來，屢詔群下勤求直言，使百僚轉對，置匭函，設直言極諫科。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty took the throne you have repeatedly issued an edict the ranks below to seek frank speech earnestly, ordered the hundred officials to rotate in audience, set up the suggestion box, and established the Straight Talk and Extreme Remonstrance examination.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty took the throne you have repeatedly urged the court to seek frank speech, ordered rotating audiences, set up the suggestion box, and established the Straight Talk examination.

sentences.zh: 今詔書頓異前事，豈非大臣雍蔽陛下聰明，杜塞忠良之口，不惟虧損朝政，實亦自取覆亡之道。

translations.literal: Now the edict suddenly differs from what went before. Is it not that great ministers have blocked Your Majesty's clarity and stopped the mouths of the loyal and good—not only harming court governance but actually taking the road to their own ruin?
translations.idiomatic: Now the edict suddenly reverses what went before. Have great ministers not blocked Your Majesty's clarity and silenced the loyal—not only harming governance but taking the road to their own ruin?

sentences.zh: 夫納善進賢，宰相之事，蔽君自任，未或不亡。

translations.literal: To accept what is good and advance the worthy is the chief minister's task; to block the ruler and act on one's own has never failed to bring ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Accepting what is good and advancing the worthy is the chief minister's task; blocking the ruler and acting on one's own has never failed to bring ruin.

sentences.zh: 今諫官、御史悉出其門，但希旨意，即獲美官，多士盈庭。

translations.literal: Now remonstrance officials and censors all come from their faction; they need only hope for their intent and at once receive fine posts, while many scholars fill the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Now remonstrance officials and censors all come from their faction; they need only follow their intent to receive fine posts. Many scholars fill the hall,

sentences.zh: 噤不得語。

translations.literal: yet are silenced and dare not speak.
translations.idiomatic: yet are silenced and dare not speak.

sentences.zh: 陛下拱默，何由盡聞天下之事乎？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty sits in silence, how can you fully hear the affairs of the realm?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty sits in silence, how can you fully hear the affairs of the realm?

sentences.zh: 前孔道輔、範仲淹剛直不撓，致位台諫，後雖改他官，不忘獻納。

translations.literal: Earlier Kong Daofu and Fan Zhongyan were upright and unyielding and rose to remonstrance posts; though later transferred to other offices, they did not forget to offer counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Kong Daofu and Fan Zhongyan were upright and unyielding and rose to remonstrance posts; though later transferred to other offices, they did not forget to offer counsel.

sentences.zh: 二臣者非不知緘口數年，坐得卿輔，蓋不敢負陛下委注之意。

translations.literal: The two men were not unaware that by keeping silent for years they could sit as chief ministers; they simply dared not betray the trust Your Majesty placed in them.
translations.idiomatic: The two men were not unaware that by keeping silent for years they could become chief ministers; they simply dared not betray the trust Your Majesty placed in them.

sentences.zh: 而皆罹中傷，竄謫而去，使正臣奪氣，鯁士咋舌，目睹時弊口不敢論。

translations.literal: Yet both suffered slander and were banished, making upright ministers lose heart and blunt men bite their tongues, seeing the ills of the age yet daring not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Yet both suffered slander and were banished, making upright ministers lose heart and blunt men bite their tongues, seeing the ills of the age yet daring not speak.

sentences.zh: 昔晉侯問叔向曰：“國家之患孰為大？”

translations.literal: In antiquity Duke Wen of Jin asked Shu Xiang, "What is the greatest affliction of a state?"
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Duke Wen of Jin asked Shu Xiang, "What is the greatest affliction of a state?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：“大臣持祿而不極諫，小臣畏罪而不敢言，下情不得上通，此患之大者。”

translations.literal: He answered, "Great ministers hold their salaries yet do not remonstrate to the limit; petty officials fear punishment and dare not speak; lower sentiments cannot reach above—this is the greatest affliction."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Great ministers hold their salaries yet do not remonstrate fully; petty officials fear punishment and dare not speak; lower sentiments cannot reach above—this is the greatest affliction."

sentences.zh: 故漢文感女子之說而肉刑是除，武帝聽三老之議而江充以族。

translations.literal: Thus Emperor Wen of Han was moved by a woman's words and abolished corporal punishment; Emperor Wu of Han heard the elders' counsel and exterminated Jiang Chong's clan.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Emperor Wen of Han was moved by a woman's words and abolished corporal punishment; Emperor Wu heard the elders' counsel and exterminated Jiang Chong's clan.

sentences.zh: 肉刑古法，江充近臣，女子三老，愚耄疏隔之至也。

translations.literal: Corporal punishment was ancient law; Jiang Chong was a close minister; women and village elders were the most foolish and remote.
translations.idiomatic: Corporal punishment was ancient law; Jiang Chong was a close minister; women and village elders were the most foolish and remote.

sentences.zh: 蓋以義之所在，賤不可忽，二君從之，後世稱聖。

translations.literal: Yet because righteousness was at stake, the lowly could not be neglected; the two rulers followed them and later ages called them sage.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because righteousness was at stake, the lowly could not be neglected; the two rulers followed them and later ages called them sage.

sentences.zh: 況國家班設爵位，列陳豪英，故當責其公忠，安可教之循默？

translations.literal: How much more when the state arrays ranks and posts and lines up heroes—should they not be charged with public loyalty? How can one teach them to keep silent?
translations.idiomatic: How much more when the state arrays ranks and posts heroes—should they not be charged with public loyalty? How can one teach them to keep silent?

sentences.zh: 賞之使諫，尚恐不言；

translations.literal: Reward them to remonstrate and one still fears they will not speak;
translations.idiomatic: Reward them to remonstrate and one still fears they will not speak;

sentences.zh: 罪其敢言，孰肯獻納？

translations.literal: punish them for daring to speak—who will offer counsel?
translations.idiomatic: Punish them for daring to speak—who will offer counsel?

sentences.zh: 物情閉塞，上位孤危，軫念於茲，可為驚怛！

translations.literal: When sentiment is blocked, the ruler above stands alone and in peril. To reflect on this is cause for alarm!
translations.idiomatic: When sentiment is blocked, the ruler above stands alone and in peril. To reflect on this is cause for alarm!

sentences.zh: 覬望陛下發德音，寢前詔，勤於采納，下及芻蕘，可以常守隆平，保全近輔。

translations.literal: Your servant hopes Your Majesty will issue a virtuous edict, set aside the prior decree, seek counsel diligently down to grass and firewood sellers, and thus may long peace be kept and the near ministers preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant hopes Your Majesty will issue a virtuous edict, set aside the prior decree, seek counsel diligently even from common folk, and thus may long peace be kept and the near ministers preserved.

sentences.zh: 尋舉進士，改光祿寺主簿，知長垣縣，遷大理評事，監在京店宅務。

translations.literal: Soon after he passed the jinshi examination, was made director in the Court of Imperial Entertainments, governed Changyuan County, was promoted to judicial reviewer, and supervised capital shop and residence affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he passed the jinshi examination, became director in the Court of Imperial Entertainments, governed Changyuan County, was promoted to judicial reviewer, and supervised capital shop and residence affairs.

sentences.zh: 康定中，河東地震，舜欽詣匭通疏曰：

translations.literal: In the Kangding era Hedong suffered an earthquake; Shunqin submitted a memorial through the suggestion box, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the Kangding era Hedong suffered an earthquake. Shunqin submitted a memorial through the suggestion box that read:

sentences.zh: 臣聞河東地大震裂，湧水壞屋廬城堞，殺民畜幾十萬，曆旬不止。

translations.literal: Your servant hears that in Hedong the earth split in a great quake, surging water destroyed houses and city walls, and people and livestock killed numbered in the hundreds of thousands, continuing for more than ten days without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant hears that in Hedong the earth split in a great quake, surging water destroyed houses and city walls, and people and livestock killed numbered in the hundreds of thousands, continuing for more than ten days without cease.

sentences.zh: 始聞惶駭疑惑。

translations.literal: At first hearing I was alarmed, terrified, and doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: At first hearing I was alarmed, terrified, and doubtful.

sentences.zh: 竊思自編策所紀前代衰微喪亂之世，亦未嚐有此大變。

translations.literal: Privately I reflect that from what the compiled records record of former ages of decline, weakness, and chaos, such a great change has never occurred.
translations.idiomatic: Privately I reflect that in the compiled records of former ages of decline and chaos, such a great change has never occurred.

sentences.zh: 今四聖接統，內外平寧，戎夷交歡，兵革偃息，固與夫衰微喪亂之世異，何災變之作反過之耶？

translations.literal: Now four sage rulers succeed one another, within and without are tranquil, barbarians are friendly, and arms are stilled—surely unlike ages of decline and chaos. Why should calamities arise that surpass them?
translations.idiomatic: Now four sage rulers succeed one another; within and without are tranquil, barbarians are friendly, and arms are stilled—surely unlike ages of decline. Why should calamities arise that surpass them?

sentences.zh: 且妖祥之興，神實尸之，各以類告，未嘗妄也。

translations.literal: Moreover, when omens and prodigies arise, the spirits truly preside; each reports by its kind and never acts without cause.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when omens arise, the spirits truly preside; each reports by its kind and never acts without cause.

sentences.zh: 天人之應，古今之鑒，大可恐懼。

translations.literal: The correspondence of Heaven and man, the mirror of past and present—greatly to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: The correspondence of Heaven and man, the mirror of past and present—greatly to be feared.

sentences.zh: 豈王者安於逸豫、信任近臣而不省政事乎？

translations.literal: Is the king secure in ease and pleasure, trusting close ministers and not examining government?
translations.idiomatic: Is the king secure in ease and pleasure, trusting close ministers and not examining government?

sentences.zh: 廟堂之上，有非才昌祿、竊弄威福而侵上事者乎？

translations.literal: In the hall of government, are there men without talent who flourish in salary, usurping authority and encroaching on the ruler's affairs?
translations.idiomatic: In the hall of government, are there men without talent who flourish in salary, usurping authority and encroaching on the ruler's affairs?

sentences.zh: 又豈施設之政有不便民者乎？

translations.literal: Or are there policies in place that do not benefit the people?
translations.idiomatic: Or are there policies in place that do not benefit the people?

sentences.zh: 深宮之中，有陰教不謹以媚道進者乎？

translations.literal: In the inner palace, are there women whose domestic teaching is not strict who advance by flattery and sorcery?
translations.idiomatic: In the inner palace, are there women whose domestic teaching is not strict who advance by flattery and sorcery?

sentences.zh: 西北羌夷有背盟犯順之心乎？

translations.literal: Among the Qiang and Yi of the northwest, is there a mind to break alliance and rebel?
translations.idiomatic: Among the Qiang and Yi of the northwest, is there a mind to break alliance and rebel?

sentences.zh: 臣從遠方來，不知近事，心疑而口不敢道也。

translations.literal: Your servant comes from afar and does not know recent affairs; I suspect in my heart but dare not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant comes from afar and does not know recent affairs; I suspect in my heart but dare not speak.

sentences.zh: 所怪者，朝廷見此大異，不修闕政，以厭天戒、安民心，默然不恤，如無事之時。

translations.literal: What is strange is that the court, seeing this great anomaly, does not repair neglected government to satisfy Heaven's warning and settle the people's hearts, but is silent and unconcerned as if nothing had happened.
translations.idiomatic: What is strange is that the court, seeing this great anomaly, does not repair neglected government to satisfy Heaven's warning and settle the people's hearts, but is silent and unconcerned as if nothing had happened.

sentences.zh: 諫官、御史不聞進牘鋪白災害之端，以開上心。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials and censors are not heard advancing memorials to lay out the beginnings of disaster and open the ruler's mind.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials and censors are not heard advancing memorials to lay out the beginnings of disaster and open the ruler's mind.

sentences.zh: 然民情洶洶，聚首橫議，鹹有憂悸之色。

translations.literal: Yet popular sentiment is turbulent; people gather and argue openly, all with a look of fear and alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Yet popular sentiment is turbulent; people gather and argue openly, all with a look of fear and alarm.

sentences.zh: 臣以世受君祿，身齒國命，涵濡惠澤，以長此軀，目睹心思，驚怛流汗，欲盡吐肝膽，以拜封奏。

translations.literal: Your servant, having received the ruler's salary for generations, shares in the fate of the state, soaked in gracious favor to grow this body, sees with the eyes and thinks in the heart, alarmed and sweating, wishing to pour out my liver and gall in a sealed memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, having received the ruler's salary for generations, shares in the fate of the state, soaked in gracious favor to grow this body, sees with the eyes and thinks in the heart, alarmed and sweating, wishing to pour out my heart in a sealed memorial.

sentences.zh: 又見範仲淹以剛直忤奸臣，言不用而身竄謫，降詔天下，不許越職言事。

translations.literal: I also saw Fan Zhongyan, for his upright firmness offending wicked ministers, his words unused and his person banished, and an edict sent throughout the realm forbidding speech outside one's office.
translations.idiomatic: I also saw Fan Zhongyan, for his upright firmness offending wicked ministers, his words unused and his person banished, and an edict sent throughout the realm forbidding speech outside one's office.

sentences.zh: 臣不避權右，必恐橫罹中傷，無補於國，因自悲嗟，不知所措。

translations.literal: Your servant does not shun the powerful on the right, yet must fear being struck down by slander without benefit to the state, and so grieves and knows not what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant does not shun the powerful, yet must fear being struck down by slander without benefit to the state, and so grieves, not knowing what to do.

sentences.zh: 既而孟春之初，雷震暴作，臣以謂國家闕失，眾臣莫敢為陛下言者，唯天丁寧以告陛下。

translations.literal: Then at the beginning of early spring thunder crashed violently. Your servant thought the state had failings that none among the ministers dared tell Your Majesty—only Heaven admonished to inform you.
translations.idiomatic: Then at the beginning of early spring thunder crashed violently. Your servant thought the state had failings that none among the ministers dared tell Your Majesty—only Heaven admonished to inform you.

sentences.zh: 陛下果能沛發明詔，許群臣皆得獻言，臣初聞之踴躍欣抃。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty could issue a bright edict in full flood, permitting all ministers to offer counsel, at first hearing I leapt for joy.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty issued a bright edict permitting all ministers to offer counsel, at first hearing I leapt for joy.

sentences.zh: 旬日間頗有言事者，其間豈無切中時病，而未聞朝廷舉而行之，是亦收虛言而不根實效也。

translations.literal: Within ten days many spoke; among them were surely points that hit the ills of the time, yet the court was not heard to adopt and carry them out—this too is to gather empty words without rooting them in real effect.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days many spoke; among them were surely points that hit the ills of the time, yet the court was not heard to adopt them—this too is to gather empty words without real effect.

sentences.zh: 臣聞唯誠可以應天，唯實可以安民，今應天不以誠，安民不以實，徒布空文，增人太息耳，將何以謝神靈而救弊亂也！

translations.literal: Your servant hears that only sincerity can respond to Heaven and only substance can settle the people. Now responding to Heaven without sincerity and settling the people without substance—only spreading empty documents and increasing men's sighs—how will you thank the spirits and rescue corrupt disorder!
translations.idiomatic: Your servant hears that only sincerity can respond to Heaven and only substance can settle the people. Now responding to Heaven without sincerity and settling the people without substance—only spreading empty documents—how will you thank the spirits and rescue corrupt disorder!

sentences.zh: 豈大臣蒙塞天聽，不為陛下行之？

translations.literal: Is it that great ministers block Heaven's hearing and will not carry them out for Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: Is it that great ministers block Heaven's hearing and will not carry them out for Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 豈言事迂闊無所取，不足行也？

translations.literal: Or are the memorials broad and impractical, nothing to adopt, not worth carrying out?
translations.idiomatic: Or are the memorials broad and impractical, nothing worth carrying out?

sentences.zh: 臣竊見綱紀隳敗，政化闕失，其事甚眾，不可概舉，謹條大者二事以聞：

translations.literal: Your servant privately sees discipline in ruins and government and teaching in failure; the matters are very many and cannot all be listed. I respectfully set forth two great matters to report:
translations.idiomatic: Your servant privately sees discipline in ruins and government and teaching in failure; the matters are very many and cannot all be listed. I respectfully set forth two great matters:

sentences.zh: 一曰正心。

translations.literal: First, rectify the heart.
translations.idiomatic: First, rectify the heart.

sentences.zh: 夫治國如治家，治家者先修己，修己者先正心，心正則神明集而萬務理。

translations.literal: Governing the state is like governing a family: the one who governs a family first cultivates himself, and the one who cultivates himself first rectifies the heart. When the heart is rectified, the spirits gather and the ten thousand affairs are ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Governing the state is like governing a family: one first cultivates oneself, and cultivating oneself begins with rectifying the heart. When the heart is rectified, the spirits gather and the ten thousand affairs are ordered.

sentences.zh: 今民間傳陛下比年稍邇俳優賤人，燕樂逾節，賜予過度。

translations.literal: Now among the people it is rumored that in recent years Your Majesty has drawn somewhat near to actors and base men, feasting beyond measure and bestowing beyond limit.
translations.idiomatic: Now among the people it is rumored that in recent years Your Majesty has drawn somewhat near to actors and base men, feasting beyond measure and bestowing beyond limit.

sentences.zh: 燕樂逾節則蕩，賜予過度則侈。

translations.literal: Feasting beyond measure leads to dissipation; bestowing beyond limit leads to extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Feasting beyond measure leads to dissipation; bestowing beyond limit leads to extravagance.

sentences.zh: 蕩則政事不親，侈則用度不足。

translations.literal: Dissipation then means government affairs are not attended to; extravagance then means expenditures are insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Dissipation means government affairs are not attended to; extravagance means expenditures are insufficient.

sentences.zh: 臣竊觀國史，見祖宗日視朝，旰昃方罷，猶坐於後苑，門有白事者，立得召對，委曲詢訪，小善必納。

translations.literal: Your servant has looked at the dynastic records and seen that the ancestors daily attended court, finishing only at dusk, then still sat in the rear garden. If someone at the gate had a matter to report, he was summoned at once for direct inquiry; even small goods were accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has looked at the dynastic records and seen that the ancestors daily attended court, finishing only at dusk, then still sat in the rear garden. If someone at the gate had a matter to report, he was summoned at once; even small goods were accepted.

sentences.zh: 真宗末年不豫，始間日視事。

translations.literal: In the last years of Emperor Zhenzong he was unwell and only then began to hold court every other day.
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of Emperor Zhenzong he was unwell and only then began to hold court every other day.

sentences.zh: 今陛下春秋鼎盛，實宵衣旰食求治之秋，而乃隔日禦殿，此政事不親也。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty is in the prime of life—the very season of rising early and sleeping late to seek order—yet you hold court only every other day. This is not attending to government.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty is in the prime of life—the very season of rising early and sleeping late to seek order—yet you hold court only every other day. This is not attending to government.

sentences.zh: 又府庫匱竭，民鮮蓋藏，誅斂科率，殆無虛日。

translations.literal: Moreover the treasuries are depleted and the people have little stored wealth; exactions and levies continue almost without a vacant day.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the treasuries are depleted and the people have little stored wealth; exactions and levies continue almost without a vacant day.

sentences.zh: 計度經費，二十倍於祖宗時，此用度不足也。

translations.literal: Calculated expenses are twenty times those of the ancestors' time—this is insufficient expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: Calculated expenses are twenty times those of the ancestors' time—this is insufficient expenditure.

sentences.zh: 政事不親，用度不足，誠國大憂。

translations.literal: Not attending to government and insufficient expenditure are truly great worries of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Not attending to government and insufficient expenditure are truly great worries of the state.

sentences.zh: 臣望陛下修己以禦人，洗心以鑒物，勤聽斷，舍燕安，放棄優諧近習之纖人，親近剛明鯁直之良士。

translations.literal: Your servant hopes Your Majesty will cultivate yourself to command others, wash the heart to mirror things, listen and decide diligently, abandon feasting and ease, cast off the petty men of actors and jesters who are close attendants, and draw near upright, bright, blunt, and straight worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant hopes Your Majesty will cultivate yourself to command others, wash the heart to mirror things, listen and decide diligently, abandon feasting and ease, cast off petty actors and jesters among close attendants, and draw near upright, blunt, and straight worthy men.

sentences.zh: 因此災變，以思永圖，則天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Because of this calamitous change, reflect on a long design—then the realm will be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this calamitous change, reflect on a long design—then the realm will be greatly fortunate.

sentences.zh: 其二曰擇賢。

translations.literal: Second, select the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Second, select the worthy.

sentences.zh: 夫明主勞於求賢而逸於任使，然盈庭之士不須盡擇，在擇一二輔臣及御史、諫官而已。

translations.literal: The enlightened ruler labors at seeking the worthy and rests in employing them; yet among the full court one need not select all—only choose one or two chief ministers and censors and remonstrance officials.
translations.idiomatic: The enlightened ruler labors at seeking the worthy and rests in employing them; yet among the full court one need not select all—only choose one or two chief ministers and censors and remonstrance officials.

sentences.zh: 陛下用人尚未慎擇。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has not yet been careful in employing men.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has not yet been careful in employing men.

sentences.zh: 昨王隨自吏部侍郎遷門下侍郎平章事，超越十資，復為上相。

translations.literal: Recently Wang Sui moved from vice director in the Ministry of Personnel to vice director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor, surpassing ten ranks, and again became chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Wang Sui moved from vice director in the Ministry of Personnel to vice director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor, surpassing ten ranks, and again became chief minister.

sentences.zh: 此乃非常之恩，必待非常之才，而隨虛庸邪諂，非輔相之器，降麻之後，物論沸騰。

translations.literal: This was an extraordinary favor and surely required extraordinary talent, yet Sui is empty, mediocre, fawning, and sycophantic—not material for a chief minister. After the appointment edict, public opinion seethed.
translations.idiomatic: This was an extraordinary favor requiring extraordinary talent, yet Sui is empty, mediocre, and sycophantic—not material for a chief minister. After the appointment edict, public opinion seethed.

sentences.zh: 故疾纏其身，災仍於國，此亦天意愛惜我朝，陛下鑒之哉！

translations.literal: Thus illness afflicted his person and disaster followed upon the state. This too is Heaven's love for our dynasty. Your Majesty, take heed!
translations.idiomatic: Thus illness afflicted his person and disaster followed upon the state. This too is Heaven's love for our dynasty. Your Majesty, take heed!

sentences.zh: 且石中立頃在朝行，以詼諧自任，士人或有宴集，必置席間，聽其語言，以資笑噱。

translations.literal: Moreover Shi Zhongli was recently in court ranks and made jest his occupation; when scholars gathered for feasts they always placed him among the seats to hear his words for laughter.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Shi Zhongli was recently in court ranks and made jest his occupation; when scholars gathered for feasts they always placed him among the seats to hear his words for laughter.

sentences.zh: 今處之近輔，不聞嘉謀，物望甚輕，人情所忽，使災害屢降而朝廷不尊，蓋近臣多非才者。

translations.literal: Now placed among close ministers, no fine counsel is heard; public expectation is very light and popular feeling neglects him, so that disasters descend repeatedly and the court is not honored—because many close ministers lack talent.
translations.idiomatic: Now placed among close ministers, no fine counsel is heard; public expectation is very light—because many close ministers lack talent, disasters descend repeatedly and the court is not honored.

sentences.zh: 陛下左右尚如此，天下官吏可知也。

translations.literal: If those at Your Majesty's side are thus, the officials of the realm can be imagined.
translations.idiomatic: If those at Your Majesty's side are thus, the officials of the realm can be imagined.

sentences.zh: 實恐遠人輕笑中國，宜即行罷免，別選賢才。

translations.literal: I truly fear distant peoples will lightly laugh at China. They should be dismissed at once and other worthy men selected.
translations.idiomatic: I truly fear distant peoples will laugh at China. They should be dismissed at once and other worthy men selected.

sentences.zh: 又張觀為御史中丞，高若訥為司諫，二人者皆登高第，頗以文詞進，而溫和軟懦，無剛鯁敢言之氣。

translations.literal: Moreover Zhang Guan is censor-in-chief and Gao Ruone is remonstrance officer. Both attained high degrees and advanced largely through literary composition, yet are mild, soft, and weak, without the spirit of blunt, firm speech.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Zhang Guan is censor-in-chief and Gao Ruone is remonstrance officer. Both attained high degrees and advanced through literary composition, yet are mild, soft, and weak, without blunt, firm speech.

sentences.zh: 斯皆執政引拔建置，欲其慎默，不敢舉揚其私，時有所言，則必暗相關說，旁人窺之，甚可笑也。

translations.literal: These were all raised and installed by the chief ministers, who wished them to be cautious and silent and not expose their private affairs. When they sometimes spoke, they surely coordinated in secret—onlookers found it very laughable.
translations.idiomatic: These were all raised by the chief ministers, who wished them cautious and silent and not to expose their private affairs. When they sometimes spoke, they surely coordinated in secret—onlookers found it laughable.

sentences.zh: 故御史、諫官之任，臣欲陛下親擇之，不令出執政門下。

translations.literal: Thus for the posts of censor and remonstrance officer your servant wishes Your Majesty to select them personally and not let them come from the chief ministers' faction.
translations.idiomatic: Thus for censors and remonstrance officers your servant wishes Your Majesty to select them personally and not from the chief ministers' faction.

sentences.zh: 台諫官既得其人，則近臣不敢為過，乃馭下之策也。

translations.literal: Once censors and remonstrance officers have the right men, close ministers dare not do wrong—this is the policy for governing subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Once censors and remonstrance officers have the right men, close ministers dare not do wrong—this is the policy for governing subordinates.

sentences.zh: 臣以謂陛下身既勤儉，輔弼、台諫又皆得人，則天下何憂不治，災異何由而生？

translations.literal: Your servant believes that if Your Majesty is diligent and frugal in person and chief ministers and remonstrance and censor posts all have the right men, what worry is there that the realm will not be governed or prodigies arise?
translations.idiomatic: Your servant believes that if Your Majesty is diligent and frugal in person and chief ministers and censor and remonstrance posts all have the right men, what worry is there that the realm will not be governed or prodigies arise?

sentences.zh: 惟陛下少留意焉。

translations.literal: Only that Your Majesty give a little attention.
translations.idiomatic: Only that Your Majesty give a little attention.

sentences.zh: 範仲淹薦其才，召試，為集賢校理，監進奏院。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan recommended his talent; he was summoned for examination and made collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and supervisor of the Memorial Transmission Office.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan recommended his talent; he was summoned for examination and made collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and supervisor of the Memorial Transmission Office.

sentences.zh: 舜欽娶宰相杜衍女，衍時與仲淹、富弼在政府，多引用一時聞人，欲更張庶事。

translations.literal: Shunqin married the daughter of Chief Councilor Du Yan. Yan was then in government with Fan and Fu Bi and largely employed men of reputation of the time, wishing to overhaul many affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shunqin married the daughter of Chief Councilor Du Yan. Yan was then in government with Fan and Fu Bi and largely employed men of reputation, wishing to overhaul many affairs.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞王拱辰等不便其所為。

translations.literal: Vice censor-in-chief Wang Gongchen and others were ill at ease with what they did.
translations.idiomatic: Vice censor-in-chief Wang Gongchen and others were ill at ease with what they did.

sentences.zh: 會進奏院祠神，舜欽與右班殿直劉巽輒用鬻故紙公錢召妓樂，間夕會賓客。

translations.literal: When the Memorial Transmission Office sacrificed to the spirits, Shunqin and Right-Ban Palace Guard Liu Xun rashly used public funds from selling old paper to summon entertainers and music, and for several evenings entertained guests.
translations.idiomatic: When the Memorial Transmission Office sacrificed to the spirits, Shunqin and Right-Ban Palace Guard Liu Xun rashly used public funds from selling old paper to summon entertainers and music, and for several evenings entertained guests.

sentences.zh: 拱辰廉得之，諷其屬魚周詢等劾奏，因欲搖動衍。

translations.literal: Gongchen investigated and got wind of it; he prompted his subordinates Yu Zhouxun and others to memorialize impeachment, thereby wishing to shake Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Gongchen investigated and learned of it; he prompted his subordinates Yu Zhouxun and others to memorialize impeachment, thereby wishing to shake Yan.

sentences.zh: 事下開封府劾治，於是舜欽與巽俱坐自盜除名，同時會者皆知名士，因緣得罪逐出四方者十餘人。

translations.literal: The matter was sent to the Kaifeng prefecture for investigation. Thereupon Shunqin and Xun were both punished for embezzlement and removed from office; those who met at the same time were all famous men, and more than ten were punished by connection and driven out to the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was sent to Kaifeng for investigation. Shunqin and Xun were both punished for embezzlement and removed from office; those present were all famous men, and more than ten were punished by connection and driven out to the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 世以爲過刻，而拱辰等方自喜曰：「吾一舉網盡矣。」

translations.literal: The age thought the punishment overly harsh, while Gongchen and the others were just pleased with themselves, saying, "With one cast of the net we have taken them all."
translations.idiomatic: The world regarded the punishment as overly harsh, while Gongchen and the others were pleased, saying, "With one cast of the net we have taken them all."

sentences.zh: 舜欽既放廢，寓於吳中，其友人韓維責以世居京師而去離都下，隔絕親交。

translations.literal: After Shunqin was dismissed he lodged in Wu. His friend Han Wei reproached him for living in the capital for generations yet leaving the capital, cutting off kin and friends.
translations.idiomatic: After Shunqin was dismissed he lodged in Wu. His friend Han Wei reproached him for living in the capital for generations yet leaving it and cutting off kin and friends.

sentences.zh: 舜欽報書曰：

translations.literal: Shunqin replied in a letter, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Shunqin replied in a letter that read:

sentences.zh: 蒙聞責以兄弟在京師，不以義相就，獨羈外數千里，自取愁苦。

translations.literal: I have heard your rebuke that my brothers are in the capital yet I did not join them in righteousness, but lingered thousands of li abroad, choosing sorrow for myself.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard your rebuke that my brothers are in the capital yet I did not join them in righteousness, but lingered thousands of li abroad, choosing sorrow for myself.

sentences.zh: 予豈無親戚之情，豈不知會合之樂也？

translations.literal: Would I lack feeling for kin? Would I not know the joy of gathering?
translations.idiomatic: Would I lack feeling for kin? Would I not know the joy of gathering?

sentences.zh: 安肯舍安逸而甘愁苦哉！

translations.literal: How could I willingly abandon ease and willingly choose sorrow!
translations.idiomatic: How could I willingly abandon ease and choose sorrow!

sentences.zh: 昨在京師，不敢犯人顏色，不敢議論時事，隨眾上下，心誌蟠屈不開，固亦極矣。

translations.literal: Yesterday in the capital I dared not offend others' expressions, dared not discuss current affairs, followed the crowd up and down, my mind coiled and unopened—already extreme indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday in the capital I dared not offend anyone's mood, dared not discuss current affairs, followed the crowd up and down, my mind coiled tight—already at the limit.

sentences.zh: 不幸適在嫌疑之地，不能決然早自引去，致不測之禍，捽去下吏，人無敢言，友仇一波，共起謗議。

translations.literal: Unluckily I was just in a place of suspicion and could not decisively withdraw early, bringing unforeseen disaster, seized and sent down to petty officials. No one dared speak; friends and foes alike rose in slander.
translations.idiomatic: Unluckily I was in a place of suspicion and could not withdraw early, bringing unforeseen disaster, seized and sent before petty officials. No one dared speak; friends and foes alike rose in slander.

sentences.zh: 被廢之後，喧然未已，更欲置之死地然後為快。

translations.literal: After dismissal the uproar did not cease; they wished to place me in the ground before they were satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: After dismissal the uproar did not cease; they wished to see me dead before they were satisfied.

sentences.zh: 來者往往鉤賾言語，欲以傳播，好意相恤者幾希矣。

translations.literal: Visitors often hooked at my words to spread them; those who meant well to comfort me were very few.
translations.idiomatic: Visitors often twisted my words to spread them; those who meant well to comfort me were very few.

sentences.zh: 故閉戶不敢與相見，如避兵寇。

translations.literal: Therefore I shut my door and dared not meet people, as if avoiding armed raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I shut my door and dared not meet people, as if avoiding armed raiders.

sentences.zh: 偷俗如此，安可久居其間！

translations.literal: Customs are so base—how could one long dwell among them!
translations.idiomatic: Customs are so base—how could one long dwell among them!

sentences.zh: 遂超然遠舉，羈泊於江湖之上，不唯衣食之累，實亦少避機阱也。

translations.literal: Thus I rose far away and drifted on rivers and lakes, not only to escape the burden of food and clothing but truly to avoid a few snares.
translations.idiomatic: Thus I rose far away and drifted on rivers and lakes, not only to escape want but truly to avoid snares.

sentences.zh: 況血屬之多，資入之薄，持國見之矣。

translations.literal: Moreover kin are many and income thin—as Chiguo has seen.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover kin are many and income thin—as Chiguo has seen.

sentences.zh: 常相團聚，可乏衣食乎？

translations.literal: If we always gathered together, could we lack food and clothing?
translations.idiomatic: If we always gathered together, could we lack food and clothing?

sentences.zh: 不可也。

translations.literal: We could not.
translations.idiomatic: We could not.

sentences.zh: 可閉關常不與人接乎？

translations.literal: Could one shut the gate and never meet people?
translations.idiomatic: Could one shut the gate and never meet people?

sentences.zh: 不可也。

translations.literal: We could not.
translations.idiomatic: We could not.

sentences.zh: 與人接必與之言，與之言必與之還往，使人人皆如持國則可，不迨持國者必加釀惡言，喧布上下，使仆不能自明，則前日之事未為重也。

translations.literal: Meeting people one must speak with them; speaking one must associate with them. If all were like Chiguo it would do; those unlike Chiguo would surely brew evil words and broadcast them above and below, so that I could not clear myself—then the affair of the other day would not be heavy.
