translations.idiomatic: Meeting people one must speak; speaking one must associate. If all were like Chiguo it would do; those unlike Chiguo would brew evil words and broadcast them, so I could not clear myself—then the affair of the other day would not even be heavy.

sentences.zh: 都無此事，亦終日勞苦，應接之不暇，寒暑奔走塵土泥淖中，不能了人事，羸馬餓仆，日棲棲取辱於都城，使人指背譏笑哀閔，亦何顏麵，安得不謂之愁苦哉！

translations.literal: None of that—yet still laboring all day, too busy to receive visitors, running through dust and mud in heat and cold, unable to finish human affairs, lean horse and hungry servant, daily restless taking insult in the capital, making people point and laugh in pity behind my back—what face to show? How not call it sorrow!
translations.idiomatic: None of that—yet still laboring all day, too busy to receive visitors, running through dust and mud in heat and cold, unable to finish affairs, lean horse and hungry servant, daily taking insult in the capital while people point and laugh behind my back—what face to show? How not call it sorrow!

sentences.zh: 此雖與兄弟親戚相遠，而伏臘稍足，居室稍寬，無終日應接奔走之勞，耳目清曠，不設機關以待人，心安閑而體舒放。

translations.literal: Though far from brothers and kin, offerings at festivals are somewhat sufficient, the dwelling somewhat spacious, without the labor of receiving visitors all day, ears and eyes clear and open, no traps set for people, the heart at ease and the body relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: Though far from brothers and kin, festival offerings are somewhat sufficient, the dwelling somewhat spacious, without all-day receiving of visitors, ears and eyes clear, no traps set for people, the heart at ease and the body relaxed.

sentences.zh: 三商而眠，高舂而起，靜院明窗之下，羅列圖史琴樽以自愉悅，有興則泛小舟出盤、閶二門，吟嘯覽古於江山之間。

translations.literal: Sleep at the third watch, rise at high morning, under quiet courtyard and bright window array books, histories, zithers, and wine cups for self-delight; when moved, pole a small boat out the Pan and Chang gates, chanting and viewing antiquity among rivers and hills.
translations.idiomatic: Sleep at the third watch, rise at high morning, under quiet courtyard and bright window array books, histories, zithers, and wine for delight; when moved, pole a small boat out the Pan and Chang gates, chanting and viewing antiquity among rivers and hills.

sentences.zh: 渚茶、野釀足以銷憂，蓴鱸、稻蟹足以適口。

translations.literal: Shore tea and country wine suffice to dispel sorrow; water shield, perch, rice, and crab suffice for the mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Shore tea and country wine suffice to dispel sorrow; water shield, perch, rice, and crab suffice for the palate.

sentences.zh: 又多高僧隱君子，佛廟勝絕，家有園林，珍花奇石，曲池高台，魚鳥留連，不覺日暮。

translations.literal: There are also many lofty monks and hidden gentlemen, Buddhist temples of surpassing beauty, family gardens, rare flowers and strange stones, winding pools and high terraces, fish and birds lingering—one does not notice sunset.
translations.idiomatic: There are also lofty monks and hidden gentlemen, surpassing Buddhist temples, family gardens, rare flowers and strange stones, winding pools and high terraces, fish and birds lingering—one does not notice sunset.

sentences.zh: 昔孔子作《春秋》而夷吳，又曰：“吾欲居九夷。”

translations.literal: In antiquity Confucius composed the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 and dwelt among the Yi of Wu, and also said, "I wish to dwell among the Nine Yi."
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Confucius composed the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 and dwelt among the Yi of Wu, and also said, "I wish to dwell among the Nine Yi."

sentences.zh: 觀今之風俗，樂善好事，知予守道好學，皆欣然願來過從，不以罪人相遇，雖孔子復生，是亦必欲居此也。

translations.literal: Viewing today's customs, people delight in good deeds, know that I keep the Way and love learning, and all gladly wish to visit—they do not treat me as a criminal. Though Confucius were reborn, he too would surely wish to dwell here.
translations.idiomatic: Viewing today's customs, people delight in good deeds, know that I keep the Way and love learning, and gladly wish to visit—they do not treat me as a criminal. Though Confucius were reborn, he too would wish to dwell here.

sentences.zh: 以彼此較之，孰為然哉！

translations.literal: Comparing the two, which is right!
translations.idiomatic: Comparing the two, which is right!

sentences.zh: 人生內有自得，外有所適，固亦樂矣，何必高位厚祿，役人以自奉養，然後為樂？

translations.literal: In life one has inner self-satisfaction and outer suitability—already joy. Why must high rank and thick salary, driving others to support oneself, then be called joy?
translations.idiomatic: In life one has inner satisfaction and outer suitability—already joy. Why must high rank and thick salary, driving others to support oneself, then be called joy?

sentences.zh: 今雖僑此，亦如仕宦南北，安可與親戚常相守耶！

translations.literal: Now though I lodge here, it is like serving in office north and south—how can one always stay with kin!
translations.idiomatic: Now though I lodge here, it is like serving in office north and south—how can one always stay with kin!

sentences.zh: 予窘迫，勢不得如持國意，必使我屍轉溝洫，肉喂豺虎，而後以為安所義，何其忍耶！

translations.literal: I am in straits and by circumstance cannot do as Chiguo wishes; you would have my corpse turn in ditches and my flesh feed jackals and tigers, then call that the righteous dwelling—how cruel!
translations.idiomatic: I am in straits and cannot do as Chiguo wishes; you would have my corpse turn in ditches and my flesh feed jackals, then call that the righteous dwelling—how cruel!

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：“凡今之人，莫如兄弟。”

translations.literal: The 《Odes》 say, "Among men today, none like brothers."
translations.idiomatic: The 《Odes》 say, "Among men today, none like brothers."

sentences.zh: 謂兄弟以恩，急難必相拯救。

translations.literal: This speaks of brothers by affection—in urgent difficulty they must rescue one another.
translations.idiomatic: This speaks of brothers by affection—in urgent difficulty they must rescue one another.

sentences.zh: 後章曰：“喪亂既平，既安且寧，雖有兄弟，不如友生。”

translations.literal: The later stanza says, "When turmoil is stilled, when there is peace and calm, though one has brothers, they are not like friends."
translations.idiomatic: The later stanza says, "When turmoil is stilled, when there is peace and calm, though one has brothers, they are not like friends."

sentences.zh: 謂友朋尚義，安寧之時，以禮義相琢磨。

translations.literal: This speaks of friends honoring righteousness—in times of peace they polish one another with ritual and right.
translations.idiomatic: This speaks of friends honoring righteousness—in times of peace they polish one another with ritual and right.

sentences.zh: 予於持國，外兄弟也。

translations.literal: Between Chiguo and me we are friends like brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Between Chiguo and me we are friends like brothers.

sentences.zh: 急難不相救，又於未安寧之際，欲以義相琢刻，雖古人所不能受，予欲不報，慮淺吾持國也。

translations.literal: In urgent difficulty you do not rescue me, and in a time not yet peaceful you wish to polish me with righteousness—though ancients could not accept this, if I do not reply I fear I slight Chiguo.
translations.idiomatic: In urgent difficulty you do not rescue me, and in a time not yet peaceful you wish to polish me with righteousness—though ancients could not accept this, if I do not reply I fear I slight Chiguo.

sentences.zh: 二年，得湖州長史，卒。

translations.literal: Two years later he received the post of recorder in Huzhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he received the post of recorder in Huzhou and died.

sentences.zh: 舜欽數上書論朝廷事，在蘇州買水石作滄浪亭，益讀書，時發憤懣於歌詩，其體豪放，往往驚人。

translations.literal: Shunqin repeatedly memorialized on court affairs. In Suzhou he bought water and rocks and built the Surging Waves Pavilion, read more, and from time to time poured indignation into songs; his style was bold and often startling.
translations.idiomatic: Shunqin repeatedly memorialized on court affairs. In Suzhou he bought water and rocks and built the Surging Waves Pavilion, read more, and poured indignation into songs; his style was bold and often startling.

sentences.zh: 善草書，每酣酒落筆，爭為人所傳。

translations.literal: He was skilled at cursive script; whenever drunk he set brush to paper, and people vied to copy and spread it.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at cursive script; whenever drunk he set brush to paper, and people vied to copy and spread it.

sentences.zh: 及謫死。

translations.literal: When banished he died.
translations.idiomatic: When banished he died.

sentences.zh: 世尤惜之。

translations.literal: The age especially mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: The age especially mourned him.

sentences.zh: 妻杜氏，有賢行。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Du had worthy conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Du had worthy conduct.

sentences.zh: 兄舜元，字才翁，為人精悍任氣節，為歌詩亦豪健，尤善草書，舜欽不能及。

translations.literal: His elder brother Shunyuan, style name Caiweng, was keen and bold in spirit; his songs were also vigorous, and he was especially skilled at cursive script—Shunqin could not match him.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Shunyuan, styled Caiweng, was keen and bold in spirit; his songs were also vigorous, and he was especially skilled at cursive script—Shunqin could not match him.

sentences.zh: 官至尚書度支員外郎、三司度支判官。

translations.literal: He reached the post of vice director in the Ministry of Revenue in the Secretariat and revenue commissioner in the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: He reached vice director in the Ministry of Revenue and revenue commissioner in the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 尹源，字子漸，少博學強記，與弟洙皆以文學知名，洙議論明辨，果於有為。

translations.literal: Yin Yuan, style name Zijian, in youth was broadly learned with a strong memory. He and his younger brother Zhu were both famed for letters; Zhu's discourse was clear and he was resolute in action.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yuan, styled Zijian, in youth was broadly learned with a strong memory. He and his younger brother Zhu were both famed for letters; Zhu's discourse was clear and he was resolute in action.

sentences.zh: 源自晦，不矜飾，有所發即過人。

translations.literal: Yuan was self-effacing and did not adorn himself; when he spoke he surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was self-effacing and did not adorn himself; when he spoke he surpassed others.

sentences.zh: 初以祖蔭補三班借職，稍遷殿直。

translations.literal: At first through his grandfather's privilege he was appointed Third-Rank Attendant on probation and was gradually promoted to palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: At first through his grandfather's privilege he was appointed Third-Rank Attendant on probation and was gradually promoted to palace guard.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，為奉禮郎，累遷太常博士，曆知芮城、河陽、新鄭三縣，通判涇州。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, became ceremonial attendant, was promoted repeatedly to erudite in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, governed the three counties of Ruicheng, Heyang, and Xinzheng, and was vice-commissioner of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, became ceremonial attendant, was promoted to erudite in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, governed Ruicheng, Heyang, and Xinzheng, and was vice-commissioner of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時知滄州劉渙坐專斬部卒，降知密州。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Huan, prefect of Cangzhou, was punished for summarily executing a subordinate soldier and was demoted to prefect of Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Liu Huan, prefect of Cangzhou, was punished for summarily executing a subordinate soldier and was demoted to prefect of Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 源上書言：“渙為主將，部卒有罪不伏，笞輒呼萬歲，渙斬之不為過。

translations.literal: Yuan memorialized, saying, "As commanding general, when a subordinate was guilty and would not submit and shouted 'Long live!' when beaten, Huan's execution was not excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan memorialized, saying, "As commanding general, when a subordinate was guilty, would not submit, and shouted 'Long live!' when beaten, Huan's execution was not excessive.

sentences.zh: 以此謫渙，臣恐邊兵愈驕，輕視主將，所係非輕也。”

translations.literal: To banish Huan for this—your servant fears frontier troops will grow more arrogant and slight their commanders; what is at stake is not light."
translations.idiomatic: To banish Huan for this—your servant fears frontier troops will grow more arrogant and slight their commanders; what is at stake is not light."

sentences.zh: 渙遂獲免。

translations.literal: Huan was thereby spared.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was thereby spared.

sentences.zh: 嚐作《唐說》及《敘兵》十篇上之。

translations.literal: He once composed the 《Discourse on Tang》 and ten chapters of 《On Military Affairs》 and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: He once composed the 《Discourse on Tang》 and ten chapters of 《On Military Affairs》 and presented them.

sentences.zh: 其《唐說》曰：

translations.literal: His 《Discourse on Tang》 says:
translations.idiomatic: His 《Discourse on Tang》 says:

sentences.zh: 世言唐所以亡，由諸侯之強，此未極於理。

translations.literal: The age says Tang perished because the feudatories were strong—this does not reach the limit of reason.
translations.idiomatic: The age says Tang perished because the feudatories were strong—this does not reach the limit of reason.

sentences.zh: 夫弱唐者，諸侯也。

translations.literal: What weakened Tang were the feudatories.
translations.idiomatic: What weakened Tang were the feudatories.

sentences.zh: 唐既弱矣，而久不亡者，諸侯維之也。

translations.literal: Once Tang was weak, yet long did not perish because the feudatories sustained it.
translations.idiomatic: Once Tang was weak, yet long did not perish because the feudatories sustained it.

sentences.zh: 燕、趙、魏首亂唐製，專地而治，若古之建國，此諸侯之雄者，然皆恃唐為輕重。

translations.literal: Yan, Zhao, and Wei first disturbed Tang's system, held territory and governed like ancient states—these were the mighty among feudatories, yet all relied on Tang for weight.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, Zhao, and Wei first disturbed Tang's system, held territory and governed like ancient states—these were the mighty among feudatories, yet all relied on Tang for weight.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 假王命以相製則易而順，唐雖病之，亦不得而外焉。

translations.literal: Borrowing the king's mandate to restrain one another was easy and orderly; though Tang was ill, it could not be cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: Borrowing the king's mandate to restrain one another was easy and orderly; though Tang was ill, it could not be cast aside.

sentences.zh: 故河北順而聽命，則天下為亂者不能遂其亂；

translations.literal: Thus when Hebei was obedient and listened to orders, those who would make trouble in the realm could not complete their trouble;
translations.idiomatic: Thus when Hebei was obedient and listened to orders, those who would make trouble in the realm could not complete their trouble;

sentences.zh: 河北不順而變，則奸雄或附而起。

translations.literal: when Hebei was disobedient and changed, then treacherous heroes might rise attached.
translations.idiomatic: when Hebei was disobedient and changed, then treacherous heroes might rise attached.

sentences.zh: 德宗世，朱泚、李希烈始遂其僭而終敗亡，田悅叛於前，武俊順於後也。

translations.literal: In Emperor Dezong's time Zhu Ci and Li Xilie first achieved their usurpation yet finally were defeated and destroyed; Tian Yue rebelled before, Wu Jun was obedient after.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Dezong's time Zhu Ci and Li Xilie first achieved their usurpation yet finally were defeated; Tian Yue rebelled before, Wu Jun was obedient after.

sentences.zh: 憲宗討蜀、平夏、誅蔡、夷鄆，兵連四方而亂不生，卒成中興之功者，田氏稟命、王承宗歸國也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong attacked Shu, pacified Xia, executed Cai, and destroyed Yun; armies linked the four quarters yet disorder did not arise—the merit of mid-dynasty revival was because the Tian clan received orders and Wang Chengzong returned to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong attacked Shu, pacified Xia, executed Cai, and destroyed Yun; armies linked the four quarters yet disorder did not arise—mid-dynasty revival was because the Tian clan received orders and Wang Chengzong returned to the state.

sentences.zh: 武宗將討劉稹之叛，先正三鎮，絕其連衡之計，而王誅以成。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong was about to attack Liu Zhen's rebellion, he first rectified the three circuits, cut off their alliance plan, and Wang's execution succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong was about to attack Liu Zhen's rebellion, he first rectified the three circuits, cut off their alliance plan, and Wang's execution succeeded.

sentences.zh: 如是二百年，奸臣逆子專國命者有之，夷將相者有之，而不敢窺神器，非力不足，畏諸侯之勢也。

translations.literal: Thus for two hundred years there were wicked ministers and rebellious sons who monopolized state power and degraded generals and ministers, yet none dared peer at the sacred vessel—not from insufficient strength but from fear of the feudatories' power.
translations.idiomatic: Thus for two hundred years wicked ministers and rebellious sons monopolized state power, yet none dared peer at the throne—not from insufficient strength but from fear of the feudatories' power.

sentences.zh: 及廣明之後，關東無復唐有，方鎮相侵伐者，猶以王室為名。

translations.literal: After the Guangming era the east of the passes no longer belonged to Tang; when circuit commissioners invaded one another they still took the royal house as their name.
translations.idiomatic: After the Guangming era the east of the passes no longer belonged to Tang; when circuit commissioners invaded one another they still took the royal house as their name.

sentences.zh: 及梁祖舉河南，劉仁恭輕戰而敗，羅氏內附，王鎔請盟，於時河北之事去矣。

translations.literal: When the Liang founder raised Henan, Liu Rengong was defeated for fighting lightly, the Luo clan submitted within, and Wang Rong requested alliance—then Hebei affairs were gone.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang founder raised Henan, Liu Rengong was defeated for fighting lightly, the Luo clan submitted within, and Wang Rong requested alliance—then Hebei affairs were settled.

sentences.zh: 梁人一舉而代唐有國，諸侯莫能與之爭，其勢然也。

translations.literal: The Liang in one move replaced Tang and held the realm; the feudatories could not contend with them—the trend was thus.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang in one move replaced Tang and held the realm; the feudatories could not contend—the trend was thus.

sentences.zh: 向使以僖、昭之弱，乘巢、蔡之亂，而田承嗣守魏，王武俊、朱滔據燕、趙，強相均，地相屬，其勢宜莫敢先動，況非義舉乎？

translations.literal: Had the weakness of Xizong and Zhaozong met the turmoil of Huang Chao and Cai Jing, while Tian Chengsi held Wei and Wang Wujun and Zhu Tao held Yan and Zhao, strong and evenly matched, territory connected—the trend should have been that none dared move first, how much less an unrighteous act?
translations.idiomatic: Had Xizong and Zhaozong's weakness met Huang Chao and Cai Jing's turmoil, while Tian Chengsi held Wei and Wang Wujun and Zhu Tao held Yan and Zhao, strong and evenly matched—the trend should have been that none dared move first, how much less an unrighteous act?

sentences.zh: 如此雖梁祖之暴，不過取霸於一方耳，安能強禪天下？

translations.literal: Thus even the Liang founder's violence would have taken hegemony in one region only—how could he forcibly yield the realm by Zen?
translations.idiomatic: Thus even the Liang founder's violence would have taken hegemony in one region only—how could he forcibly yield the realm by Zen?

sentences.zh: 故唐之弱者，以河北之強也；

translations.literal: Thus Tang was weak because Hebei was strong;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Tang was weak because Hebei was strong;

sentences.zh: 唐之亡者，以河北之弱也。

translations.literal: Tang perished because Hebei was weak.
translations.idiomatic: Tang perished because Hebei was weak.

sentences.zh: 或曰：“諸侯強則分天子之勢，子何議之過乎？”

translations.literal: Someone said, "When feudatories are strong they divide the Son of Heaven's power—why do you argue excessively?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "When feudatories are strong they divide the Son of Heaven's power—why argue excessively?"

sentences.zh: 曰：“秦、隋之勢無分於諸侯，而亡速於唐，何如哉？”

translations.literal: He answered, "Qin and Sui had no division among feudatories yet perished faster than Tang—how is that?"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Qin and Sui had no division among feudatories yet perished faster than Tang—how is that?"

sentences.zh: 或曰：“唐之亡其由君失道乎？”

translations.literal: Another said, "Did Tang perish because the ruler lost the Way?"
translations.idiomatic: Another said, "Did Tang perish because the ruler lost the Way?"

sentences.zh: 曰：“君非失道，而才不至焉爾，其亡也，臣實主之。”

translations.literal: He said, "The ruler did not lose the Way but talent did not reach it; its perishing was really led by ministers."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "The ruler did not lose the Way but talent did not reach it; its perishing was really led by ministers."

sentences.zh: 請極其說：唐太宗起艱難有天下，其用臣也，聽其言而盡其才，故君臣相親而至治安。

translations.literal: Please carry the argument to the limit: Emperor Taizong rose from hardship to gain the realm; in employing ministers he heard their words and exhausted their talents, so ruler and minister were close and reached peace and order.
translations.idiomatic: Please carry the argument to the limit: Emperor Taizong rose from hardship to gain the realm; in employing ministers he heard their words and exhausted their talents, so ruler and minister were close and reached peace and order.

sentences.zh: 以及後世，視太宗由茲而興，雖其聖不及，而任臣納諫之心一也。

translations.literal: Down to later generations, viewing Taizong's rise from this, though their sagehood did not reach his, the heart to employ ministers and accept remonstrance was one.
translations.idiomatic: Down to later generations, viewing Taizong's rise from this, though their sagehood did not reach his, the heart to employ ministers and accept remonstrance was one.

sentences.zh: 君有太宗之心，臣非太宗之臣，上聽其下，或不能辨其奸，下惑其上，無所不至，所以敗也。

translations.literal: The ruler had Taizong's heart but ministers were not Taizong's ministers; above he listened to below, or could not distinguish treachery; below they deluded above without limit—thus defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler had Taizong's heart but ministers were not Taizong's ministers; above he listened to below, or could not distinguish treachery; below they deluded above without limit—thus defeat.

sentences.zh: 何哉？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 夫君一而臣眾，大聖之君不相繼而出，大奸之臣則世有之。

translations.literal: One ruler and many ministers—a sage ruler does not succeed in unbroken line, but great traitorous ministers appear in every age.
translations.idiomatic: One ruler and many ministers—a sage ruler does not succeed in unbroken line, but great traitorous ministers appear in every age.

sentences.zh: 大聖在上，則奸無所容，其臣莫不賢。

translations.literal: When a great sage is above, treachery has no place and his ministers are all worthy.
translations.idiomatic: When a great sage is above, treachery has no place and his ministers are all worthy.

sentences.zh: 苟君之才不能勝臣之奸，則雖有賢者不能進矣。

translations.literal: If the ruler's talent cannot overcome the ministers' treachery, then though there are worthy men they cannot advance.
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler's talent cannot overcome the ministers' treachery, then though there are worthy men they cannot advance.

sentences.zh: 如是，然未至於失道，猶失道也。

translations.literal: Thus though not yet reaching loss of the Way, it is still loss of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Thus though not yet reaching loss of the Way, it is still loss of the Way.

sentences.zh: 明皇非不欲天下如貞觀之治，而馭臣之才不能勝林甫之奸，於是有祿山之禍。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming did not lack the wish to make the realm like the Zhenguan order, but his talent for controlling ministers could not overcome Li Linfu's treachery—thus the disaster of An Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming did not lack the wish to make the realm like the Zhenguan order, but his talent for controlling ministers could not overcome Li Linfu's treachery—thus the disaster of An Lushan.

sentences.zh: 德宗非不欲平暴亂、安四方，而君人之術不能勝盧杞之邪，於是有朱泚之變。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong did not lack the wish to pacify violence and settle the four quarters, but his art of ruling could not overcome Lu Qi's evil—thus Zhu Ci's rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong did not lack the wish to pacify violence and settle the four quarters, but his art of ruling could not overcome Lu Qi's evil—thus Zhu Ci's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 以至於僖、昭，其心皆欲去亂而即治也，而才不逮於明皇、德宗，輔臣之奸邪或過於林甫、盧杞，求國不亡，安可得已！

translations.literal: Down to Xizong and Zhaozong their hearts all wished to remove disorder and reach order, but talent did not reach Ming and Dezong and the treachery of assisting ministers equaled or exceeded Linfu and Qi—seeking that the state not perish, how could it be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: Down to Xizong and Zhaozong their hearts all wished to remove disorder and reach order, but talent did not reach Ming and Dezong and assisting ministers' treachery equaled or exceeded Linfu and Qi—seeking that the state not perish, how could it be obtained!

sentences.zh: 然跡其事，君豈有失道乎？

translations.literal: Yet tracing the matter, did the ruler lose the Way?
translations.idiomatic: Yet tracing the matter, did the ruler lose the Way?

sentences.zh: 於時天下非無賢，由君不能主聽也。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was not without worthies—it was because the ruler could not preside and listen.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the realm was not without worthies—it was because the ruler could not preside and listen.

sentences.zh: 故至賢之主與夫失道之主，其興其亡，皆自取之，此係乎君者也。

translations.literal: Thus whether a most worthy ruler or a ruler who lost the Way, their rise and fall are taken by themselves—this depends on the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Thus whether a most worthy ruler or a ruler who lost the Way, their rise and fall are taken by themselves—this depends on the ruler.

sentences.zh: 中才之主，其臣正勝邪則治而安，邪勝正則亂而亡，此係乎臣者也。

translations.literal: A ruler of middling talent: if his upright ministers overcome the wicked, there is order and peace; if the wicked overcome the upright, there is disorder and perishing—this depends on ministers.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler of middling talent: if upright ministers overcome the wicked, there is order and peace; if the wicked overcome the upright, there is disorder and perishing—this depends on ministers.

sentences.zh: 然則唐之亡非君之為，臣之為也。

translations.literal: Thus Tang's perishing was not the ruler's doing but the ministers' doing.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Tang's perishing was not the ruler's doing but the ministers' doing.

sentences.zh: 其《敘兵》曰：

translations.literal: His 《On Military Affairs》 says:
translations.idiomatic: His 《On Military Affairs》 says:

sentences.zh: 唐杜牧當會昌中河朔用兵，嚐為文數篇，上論曆代軍事利害，繼以本朝製兵、用將之得失，下參以當時事機。

translations.literal: Tang Du Mu, during the Huichang era when Hebei used troops, once wrote several essays discussing the military advantages and harms of successive ages, continuing with the gains and losses of the present dynasty in organizing troops and employing generals, and below comparing with the circumstances of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Du Mu, during the Huichang era when Hebei used troops, wrote several essays on military advantages and harms through the ages, on the present dynasty's organizing troops and employing generals, and on circumstances of the time.

sentences.zh: 牧，儒者，位不顯，其術未嚐試，然識者謂牧知兵，雖古名將不能過。

translations.literal: Mu was a Confucian, his rank not prominent, his methods not tried, yet connoisseurs said Mu understood warfare—even ancient famed generals could not surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: Mu was a Confucian, his rank not prominent, his methods not tried, yet connoisseurs said Mu understood warfare—even ancient famed generals could not surpass him.

sentences.zh: 今觀牧所著，大要究極當世之務，不專狃古法，使時君可行而易為功，此其善也。

translations.literal: Now viewing what Mu wrote, in the main he exhaustively investigates affairs of the age, not clinging only to ancient methods, making them feasible for the ruler of the time and easy to achieve merit—this is his excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Now viewing what Mu wrote, in the main he exhaustively investigates affairs of the age, not clinging only to ancient methods, making them feasible for the ruler and easy to achieve merit—this is his excellence.

sentences.zh: 今兵之利鈍所以與唐世異者，唐自中世以來，諸侯皆自募兵訓練，出攻入守，上下一誌，故討淮西、青、冀、滄德、澤潞之叛，以至四征夷狄，大率假外兵以集事，朝廷所出神策禁軍，不過為聲援而已，故所至多有功。

translations.literal: Now the sharp and dull of troops differ from the Tang age because from mid-Tang the feudatories all recruited and trained their own troops for attack and defense with one will above and below. Thus in campaigns against Huaixi, Qing, Ji, Cangde, Zelu rebellions and in the four expeditions against barbarians, they largely borrowed outer troops to gather affairs; the Divine Strategy Army sent out by the court was mostly vocal support—thus they often had merit where they went.
translations.idiomatic: Now troops differ from the Tang age because from mid-Tang feudatories recruited and trained their own troops with one will. Thus in campaigns against rebellions and barbarians they largely borrowed outer troops; the Divine Strategy Army was mostly vocal support—thus they often had merit.

sentences.zh: 今則不然，國家患前世藩鎮之強，凡天下所募驍勇，一萃於京師。

translations.literal: Now it is not so. The state fears the strength of former military commissioners; all the realm's valiant recruits are gathered in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Now it is not so. The state fears former military commissioners' strength; all valiant recruits are gathered in the capital.

sentences.zh: 雖濱塞諸郡，大者籍兵不逾數千，每歲防秋，則戍以禁兵，將師任輕而勢分，軍事往往中禦。

translations.literal: Though border prefectures, the largest register no more than several thousand troops; each year for autumn defense they garrison with forbidden troops; commanders' duties are light and power divided, and military affairs are often controlled from the center.
translations.idiomatic: Though border prefectures, the largest register no more than several thousand troops; each year for autumn defense they garrison with forbidden troops; commanders' duties are light and power divided, and military affairs are often controlled from the center.

sentences.zh: 愚謂此可以施於無事時，鎮中國，服豪傑心，苟戎夷侵軼，未必能取勝也。

translations.literal: I foolishly believe this can be applied in times without affairs to steady China and win heroes' hearts; if barbarians invade and raid, victory is not certain.
translations.idiomatic: I believe this can be applied in peaceful times to steady China and win heroes' hearts; if barbarians invade, victory is not certain.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 兵主於外則勇，主於內則驕，勇生於勞，驕生於逸。

translations.literal: Troops based outside are brave; based inside they are arrogant. Bravery is born from labor; arrogance from ease.
translations.idiomatic: Troops based outside are brave; based inside they are arrogant. Bravery is born from labor; arrogance from ease.

sentences.zh: 夫外兵所習尚皆疆埸戰鬥勞苦之事，死生之命製之於將，故勇，勇而使之戰則多利；

translations.literal: Outer troops' practices are all frontier battle and labor; life and death are controlled by the general—thus brave; brave and sent to battle, mostly profitable;
translations.idiomatic: Outer troops' practices are frontier battle and labor; life and death are controlled by the general—thus brave; brave and sent to battle, mostly profitable;

sentences.zh: 內兵居京師，日享安逸，加之以賞賚，未嚐服甲胄、荷戈戟，不知將帥號令之嚴，故驕，驕而勞之則怨，以之戰則多鈍。

translations.literal: inner troops dwell in the capital, daily enjoying ease, with rewards added, never having worn armor or borne halberds, not knowing the severity of generals' orders—thus arrogant; arrogant and labored, they resent; sent to battle, mostly dull.
translations.idiomatic: inner troops dwell in the capital, daily enjoying ease, with rewards added, never having worn armor or borne halberds, not knowing generals' severity—thus arrogant; arrogant and labored, they resent; sent to battle, mostly dull.

sentences.zh: 若唐之失，失於諸侯之不製，非失於外兵之強，故有驕將，罕聞有驕兵。

translations.literal: Tang's failure was failure to control the feudatories, not failure from outer troops being strong—thus there were arrogant generals but rarely arrogant soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Tang failed because feudatories were not controlled, not because outer troops were too strong—thus there were arrogant generals but rarely arrogant soldiers.

sentences.zh: 今之失，失於將太輕，而外兵不足以應敵，內兵鮮得其用，故有驕兵，不聞有驕將。

translations.literal: Today's failure is failure from generals being too light and outer troops insufficient to meet the enemy, inner troops rarely put to use—thus there are arrogant soldiers but one does not hear of arrogant generals.
translations.idiomatic: Today's failure is that generals count for too little, outer troops cannot meet the enemy, and inner troops are rarely used—thus there are arrogant soldiers but rarely arrogant generals.

sentences.zh: 且唐之所失者勢也，今之所失者制也。

translations.literal: Moreover, what the Tang lost was momentum; what is being lost today is system.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, what the Tang lost was momentum; what is being lost today is system.

sentences.zh: 勢也者，不得已也；

translations.literal: As for momentum, it could not be helped;
translations.idiomatic: As for momentum, it was beyond remedy;

sentences.zh: 制也者，可為而不為也。

translations.literal: as for system, it is something that could be acted on but is not acted on.
translations.idiomatic: as for system, it is something that could be put in order but has not been.

sentences.zh: 然則為今之計當如何？

translations.literal: Then what should today's plan be?
translations.idiomatic: Then what should today's plan be?

sentences.zh: 曰：“稍革舊制，大募豪勇，益外兵之籍，俾足以戰敵。

translations.literal: It is said, "Slightly reform the old system, greatly recruit bold warriors, increase outer troop registers so they suffice to fight the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The answer: "Slightly reform the old system, greatly recruit bold warriors, increase outer troop registers so they suffice to fight the enemy.

sentences.zh: 以內兵為聲勢，重邊將之任，使專一軍之事，而不得連州郡之勢，斯可以獲近利而亡後害也。”

translations.literal: Use inner troops as vocal support, weight frontier generals' duties so they specialize in one army's affairs and cannot link prefectural power—then near profit may be gained without later harm."
translations.idiomatic: Use inner troops as vocal support, weight frontier generals' duties so they specialize in one army and cannot link prefectural power—then near profit may be gained without later harm."

sentences.zh: 餘文多不錄。

translations.literal: The rest of the text is mostly not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder of the text is mostly omitted.

sentences.zh: 趙元昊寇定川堡，葛懷敏發涇原兵救之，源是時通判慶州，遺懷敏書曰：“賊舉國而來，其利不在城堡，而兵法有不得而救者，宜駐兵瓦亭，擇利而後動。”

translations.literal: When Zhao Yuanhao attacked Dingchuan Fort, Ge Huaimin sent Jingyuan troops to rescue. Yuan at the time was vice-commissioner of Qingzhou and sent Huaimin a letter saying, "The bandits come with the whole state; their profit is not in castles, and in military law there are times when one must not rescue. It is fitting to station troops at Wating and move after choosing advantage."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Yuanhao attacked Dingchuan Fort, Ge Huaimin sent Jingyuan troops to rescue. Yuan, then vice-commissioner of Qingzhou, wrote Huaimin: "The enemy comes with the whole state; their aim is not the fort, and military law sometimes forbids rescue. Station at Wating and move when advantage appears."

sentences.zh: 懷敏不聽，以敗。

translations.literal: Huaimin did not listen and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Huaimin did not listen and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 範仲淹、韓琦薦其才，召試學士院。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan and Han Qi recommended his talent; he was summoned for examination at the Academy of Scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan and Han Qi recommended his talent; he was summoned for examination at the Academy of Scholars.

sentences.zh: 源素不喜賦，請以論易賦，主試者方以賦進，不悅其言，第其文下，除知懷州，卒。

translations.literal: Yuan had never liked fu; he asked to substitute discourse for fu. The chief examiner was then advancing fu and disliked his words, ranked his essay low, appointed him prefect of Huaizhou, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan disliked fu and asked to substitute discourse for fu. The chief examiner was advancing fu, disliked his words, ranked his essay low, appointed him prefect of Huaizhou, and he died.

sentences.zh: 黃亢，字清臣，建州浦城人也。

translations.literal: Huang Kang, style name Qingchen, was a man of Pucheng in Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Kang, styled Qingchen, was from Pucheng in Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 母夢星殞於懷，掬而吞之，遂有娠。

translations.literal: His mother dreamed a star fell into her bosom; she scooped and swallowed it and then conceived.
translations.idiomatic: His mother dreamed a star fell into her bosom; she scooped it up and swallowed it, then conceived.

sentences.zh: 少奇穎過人，年十五，以文謁翰林學士章得象，得象奇之。

translations.literal: In youth he was extraordinarily clever. At fifteen he presented writings to Hanlin academician Zhang Dexiang, who marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was extraordinarily clever. At fifteen he presented writings to Hanlin academician Zhang Dexiang, who marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 遊錢塘，以詩贈處士林逋，逋尤激賞。

translations.literal: Traveling to Qiantang he presented a poem to the recluse Lin Bu, who especially admired it.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling to Qiantang he presented a poem to the recluse Lin Bu, who especially admired it.

sentences.zh: 時王隨知杭州，奏禁西湖為放生池，亢作詩數百言以諷，士人爭傳之。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Sui governed Hangzhou and memorialized to forbid West Lake as a release-life pond. Kang composed several hundred words of verse to satirize it, and scholars vied to spread it.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sui governed Hangzhou he memorialized to make West Lake a release-life pond. Kang composed several hundred words of verse to satirize it, and scholars vied to spread it.

sentences.zh: 亢為人侏儒，不飾小節，對人野率，如不能言。

translations.literal: Kang was a dwarf in stature, did not adorn small matters, and toward people was wild and blunt as if unable to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Kang was short in stature, careless of small manners, and toward people was wild and blunt as if unable to speak.

sentences.zh: 然嗜學強記，為文詞奇偉。

translations.literal: Yet he loved learning and had a strong memory; his literary words were strange and grand.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he loved learning and had a strong memory; his writing was strange and grand.

sentences.zh: 卒，鄉人類其文為十二卷，號《東溪集》。

translations.literal: When he died, fellow townsmen compiled his writings in twelve fascicles titled the 《Eastern Brook Collection》.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, fellow townsmen compiled his writings in twelve fascicles titled the 《Eastern Brook Collection》.

sentences.zh: 黃鑒，字唐卿，與亢同鄉里，少敏慧過人。

translations.literal: Huang Jian, style name Tangqing, was from the same village as Kang and in youth was clever beyond others.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Jian, styled Tangqing, was from the same village as Kang and in youth was clever beyond others.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，補桂陽監判官，為國子監直講。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed assistant magistrate at Guiyang Salt Office, and became lecturer in the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed assistant magistrate at Guiyang Salt Office, and became lecturer in the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 同郡楊億尤善其文詞，延置門下，由是知名。

translations.literal: Yang Yi of the same prefecture especially favored his literary words and kept him in his household, and thereby he became known.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi of the same prefecture especially favored his writing and kept him in his household, and thereby he became known.

sentences.zh: 累遷太常博士，為國史院編修官。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to erudite in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and compiler in the National History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted repeatedly to erudite in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and compiler in the National History Institute.

sentences.zh: 嚐詔館閣官後苑賞花，而鑒特預召。

translations.literal: Once an edict summoned Hall officials to view flowers in the rear garden, and Jian was specially called.
translations.idiomatic: Once an edict summoned Hall officials to view flowers in the rear garden, and Jian was specially summoned.

sentences.zh: 國史成，擢直集賢院。

translations.literal: When the national history was completed he was promoted to academician in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: When the national history was completed he was promoted to academician in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 以母老，出通判蘇州，卒。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old he went out as vice-commissioner of Suzhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother was old he went out as vice-commissioner of Suzhou and died.

sentences.zh: 楊蟠，字公濟，章安人也。

translations.literal: Yang Pan, style name Gongji, was a man of Zhang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Pan, styled Gongji, was from Zhang'an.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，為密、和二州推官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was judicial aide in Mi and He prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was judicial aide in Mi and He prefectures.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修稱其詩。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu praised his poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu praised his poetry.

sentences.zh: 蘇軾知杭州，蟠通判州事，與軾倡酬居多。

translations.literal: When Su Shi governed Hangzhou, Pan was vice-commissioner of the prefecture and often exchanged poems with Shi.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Shi governed Hangzhou, Pan was vice-commissioner and often exchanged poems with Shi.

sentences.zh: 平生為詩數千篇，後知壽州，卒。

translations.literal: In life he composed several thousand poems; later he governed Shouzhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: In life he composed several thousand poems; later he governed Shouzhou and died.

sentences.zh: 顏太初，字醇之，徐州彭城人，顏子四十七世孫。

translations.literal: Yan Taichu, style name Chunzhi, was a man of Pengcheng in Xuzhou, forty-seventh-generation descendant of Yanzi.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Taichu, styled Chunzhi, was from Pengcheng in Xuzhou, forty-seventh-generation descendant of Yanzi.

sentences.zh: 少博學，有雋才，慷慨好義。

translations.literal: In youth he was broadly learned with outstanding talent, generous and fond of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was broadly learned with outstanding talent, generous and fond of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 喜為詩，多譏切時事。

translations.literal: He delighted in composing poetry and often satirized current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in composing poetry and often satirized current affairs.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，亳州衛真令黎德潤為吏誣構，死獄中，太初以詩發其冤，覽者壯之。

translations.literal: In the Tiansheng era Li Derun, magistrate of Weizhen in Bozhou, was framed by clerks and died in prison. Taichu used a poem to expose his injustice, and readers were stirred.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiansheng era Li Derun, magistrate of Weizhen in Bozhou, was framed by clerks and died in prison. Taichu used a poem to expose his injustice, and readers were stirred.

sentences.zh: 文宣公孔聖祐卒，無子，除襲封且十年。

translations.literal: Duke Wenxuan Kong Shengyou died without sons; the hereditary enfeoffment had been vacant nearly ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wenxuan Kong Shengyou died without sons; the hereditary enfeoffment had been vacant nearly ten years.

sentences.zh: 是時有醫許希以針愈仁宗疾，拜賜已，西向拜扁鵲曰“不敢忘師也！”

translations.literal: At the time the physician Xu Xi cured Emperor Renzong's illness with needles. After receiving reward he bowed west toward Bian Que, saying, "I dare not forget my teacher!"
translations.idiomatic: At the time the physician Xu Xi cured Emperor Renzong's illness with needles. After receiving reward he bowed west toward Bian Que, saying, "I dare not forget my teacher!"

sentences.zh: 帝為封扁鵲神應侯，立祠城西。

translations.literal: The emperor enfeoffed Bian Que as Marquis of Divine Response and established a shrine west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor enfeoffed Bian Que as Marquis of Divine Response and established a shrine west of the city.

sentences.zh: 太初作《許希詩》，指聖祐事以諷在位，又致書參知政事蔡齊，齊為言於上，遂以聖祐弟襲封。

translations.literal: Taichu composed the 《Xu Xi Poem》, pointing at Shengyou's affair to satirize those in office, and also wrote Vice Grand Councilor Cai Qi; Qi spoke to the emperor, and Shengyou's younger brother received the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Taichu composed the 《Xu Xi Poem》, pointing at Shengyou's affair to satirize those in office, and wrote Vice Grand Councilor Cai Qi; Qi spoke to the emperor, and Shengyou's younger brother received the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 山東人範諷、石延年、劉潛之徒喜豪放劇飲，不循禮法，後生多慕之，太初作《東州逸黨詩》，孔道輔深器之。

translations.literal: Men of Shandong such as Fan Feng, Shi Yannian, and Liu Qian delighted in bold drinking and did not follow ritual; many younger men admired them. Taichu composed the 《Eastern Province Roaming Party Poem》; Kong Daofu deeply valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Men of Shandong such as Fan Feng, Shi Yannian, and Liu Qian delighted in bold drinking and scorned ritual; many younger men admired them. Taichu composed the 《Eastern Province Roaming Party Poem》; Kong Daofu deeply valued him.

sentences.zh: 太初中進士後，為莒縣尉，因事忤轉運使，投劾去。

translations.literal: After Taichu passed the jinshi examination he was assistant magistrate of Ju County; he offended the transport commissioner over an affair and submitted impeachment of himself and left.
translations.idiomatic: After Taichu passed the jinshi he was assistant magistrate of Ju County; he offended the transport commissioner and submitted impeachment of himself and left.

sentences.zh: 久之，補閬中主簿。

translations.literal: After a long while he was appointed recorder in Langzhong.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was appointed recorder in Langzhong.

sentences.zh: 時範諷以罪貶，同黨皆坐斥，齊與道輔薦太初，上其嚐所為詩，召試中書，言者以為此嘲譏之辭，遂報改臨晉主簿。

translations.literal: At the time Fan Feng was banished for a crime and his faction were all punished and expelled. Qi and Daofu recommended Taichu; they presented poems he had written; he was summoned for examination at the Secretariat. Critics said these were mocking words, and he was reassigned recorder in Linjin.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Feng was banished and his faction expelled, Qi and Daofu recommended Taichu and presented his poems; he was summoned for examination at the Secretariat. Critics said these were mocking words, and he was reassigned recorder in Linjin.

sentences.zh: 前此有太常博士宋武通判同州，與守爭事，恚死，守憾之，捃構其子以罪，發狂亦死，父子寓骨僧舍。

translations.literal: Earlier Erudite Song Wu was vice-commissioner of Tongzhou and quarreled with the prefect, died of resentment, and the prefect resented him and framed his son, who went mad and also died. Father and son's bones lodged in a monks' lodging.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Erudite Song Wu was vice-commissioner of Tongzhou and quarreled with the prefect, died of resentment, and the prefect framed his son, who went mad and died. Father and son's bones lodged in a monks' lodging.

sentences.zh: 時守方貴顯，無敢爲直冤。

translations.literal: The prefect was then noble and prominent; none dared seek straight justice.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect was then noble and prominent; none dared seek justice.

sentences.zh: 太初因事至同州，葬武父子，蘇舜欽於墓左。

translations.literal: Taichu on business reached Tongzhou, buried Wu father and son, and Su Shunqin was at the tomb's left.
translations.idiomatic: Taichu reached Tongzhou on business, buried Wu father and son, and Su Shunqin was at the left of the tomb.

sentences.zh: 後移應天府戶曹參軍、南京國子監說書，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was moved to revenue aide in Yingtianfu and lecturer in the Nanjing Directorate of Education, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was revenue aide in Yingtianfu and lecturer in the Nanjing Directorate of Education, and died.

sentences.zh: 著書號《洙南子》，所居在鳧、繹兩山之間，號鳧繹處士。

translations.literal: His book was titled the 《Zhushu Nanzi》; his dwelling lay between Mount Fu and Mount Yi, and he styled himself Recluse of Fu and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His book was titled the 《Zhushu Nanzi》; his dwelling lay between Mount Fu and Mount Yi, and he styled himself Recluse of Fu and Yi.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷，《淳曜聯英》二十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collection in ten fascicles and the 《Pure Radiance Linked Flowers》 in twenty fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: He had a collection in ten fascicles and the 《Pure Radiance Linked Flowers》 in twenty fascicles.

sentences.zh: 子復，嘉祐中，本郡敦遣至京師，召試舍人院，為奉議郎。

translations.literal: His son Fu, in the Jiayou era, was urged by the prefecture to the capital, summoned for examination at the Academy of Scholars, and made Gentleman for Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu, in the Jiayou era, was urged by the prefecture to the capital, summoned for examination at the Academy of Scholars, and made Gentleman for Discussion.

sentences.zh: 郭忠恕，字恕先，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Guo Zhongshu, style name Shuxian, was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhongshu, styled Shuxian, was from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 七歲能誦書屬文，舉童子及第，尤工篆籀。

translations.literal: At seven he could recite books and compose prose, passed the child prodigy examination, and was especially skilled at seal script.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he could recite books and compose prose, passed the child prodigy examination, and was especially skilled at seal script.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，漢湘陰公召之，忠恕拂衣遽辭去。

translations.literal: At twenty the Duke of Xiangyin in Han summoned him; Zhongshu shook out his robe and hastily declined.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty the Duke of Xiangyin in Han summoned him; Zhongshu shook out his robe and hastily declined.

sentences.zh: 周廣順中，召為宗正丞兼國子書學博士，改《周易》博士。

translations.literal: In the Guangshun era of Zhou he was summoned as vice director of the Court of the Imperial Clan and concurrently erudite of calligraphy in the Directorate of Education, and was changed to erudite of the 《Changes》.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangshun era of Zhou he was summoned as vice director of the Court of the Imperial Clan and concurrently erudite of calligraphy in the Directorate of Education, and was changed to erudite of the 《Changes》.

sentences.zh: 建隆初，被酒與監察御史符昭文競於朝堂，御史彈奏，忠恕叱台吏奪其奏，毀之，坐貶為乾州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianlong, drunk he competed with investigating censor Fu Zhaowen in the court hall. The censor memorialized impeachment; Zhongshu shouted at the clerks, seized the memorial, and destroyed it. He was punished and demoted to revenue aide in Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianlong, drunk he competed with investigating censor Fu Zhaowen in the court hall. The censor memorialized impeachment; Zhongshu shouted at the clerks, seized the memorial, and destroyed it. He was demoted to revenue aide in Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 乘醉毆從事範滌，擅離貶所，削籍配隸靈武。

translations.literal: Drunk he beat aide Fan Yi, left his place of banishment without permission, was struck from the rolls and assigned to Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk he beat aide Fan Yi, left his place of banishment without permission, was struck from the rolls and assigned to Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 其後，流落不復求仕進，多遊岐、雍、京、洛間，縱酒跅弛，逢人無貴賤輒呼“苗”。

translations.literal: Afterward he drifted and no longer sought office, traveling much among Qi, Yong, Jing, and Luo, drinking freely and unrestrained, meeting people without regard to rank and always calling them "Miao."
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he drifted and no longer sought office, traveling among Qi, Yong, Jing, and Luo, drinking freely and unrestrained, calling everyone "Miao" regardless of rank.

sentences.zh: 有佳山水即淹留，浹旬不能去。

translations.literal: Where there was fine landscape he lingered and could not leave for more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Where there was fine landscape he lingered and could not leave for more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 或逾月不食。

translations.literal: Sometimes he went a month without eating.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he went a month without eating.

sentences.zh: 盛暑暴露日中，體不沾汗，窮冬鑿河水而浴，其傍淩澌消釋，人皆異之。

translations.literal: In great heat he exposed himself in the sun and his body did not sweat; in deep winter he broke river ice to bathe, and the ice beside him melted—people all marveled.
translations.idiomatic: In great heat he exposed himself in the sun without sweating; in deep winter he broke river ice to bathe, and the ice beside him melted—people marveled.

sentences.zh: 尤善畫，所圖屋室重復之狀，頗極精妙。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled at painting; the layered forms of buildings he depicted were extremely refined.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled at painting; the layered forms of buildings he depicted were extremely refined.

sentences.zh: 多遊王侯公卿家，或待以美醞，豫張紈素倚於壁，乘興即畫之，苟意不欲而固請之，必怒而去，得者藏以為寶。

translations.literal: He often visited the houses of kings, marquises, and high ministers. Some treated him with fine wine and spread silk beforehand against the wall; when moved he painted at once. If he did not wish and they pressed, he would rage and leave; those who obtained his works treasured them as gems.
translations.idiomatic: He often visited noble houses. Some treated him with fine wine and spread silk against the wall; when moved he painted at once. If they pressed when he did not wish, he raged and left; those who obtained his works treasured them.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，聞其名，召赴闕，授國子監主簿，賜襲衣、銀帶、錢五萬，館於太學，令刊定曆代字書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne he heard his name, summoned him to court, appointed him director in the Directorate of Education, bestowed court robe, silver belt, and fifty thousand cash, lodged him in the Directorate of Education, and ordered him to collate successive dynasties' character books.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong took the throne he heard his name, summoned him, appointed him director in the Directorate of Education, bestowed court robe, silver belt, and fifty thousand cash, lodged him in the Directorate, and ordered him to collate successive dynasties' character books.

sentences.zh: 忠恕性無檢局，放縱敗度，上憐其才，每優容之。

translations.literal: Zhongshu's nature lacked restraint; he was unrestrained and exceeded measure. The emperor pitied his talent and always treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu lacked restraint and exceeded measure. The emperor pitied his talent and always treated him with forbearance.

sentences.zh: 益使酒，肆言謗讟，時擅鬻官物取其直，詔減死，決杖流登州。

translations.literal: He drank still more and spoke slander freely, at times privately selling official goods for their price. An edict reduced death to beating with the staff and exile to Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He drank still more and spoke slander freely, at times privately selling official goods. An edict reduced death to beating with the staff and exile to Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 時太平興國二年。

translations.literal: This was in the second year of Taiping Xingguo.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the second year of Taiping Xingguo.

sentences.zh: 已行至齊州臨邑，謂部送吏曰：“我今逝矣！”

translations.literal: Already having reached Linyi in Qizhou on the road, he said to the escort officer, "I depart today!"
translations.idiomatic: Already at Linyi in Qizhou on the road, he said to the escort officer, "I depart today!"

sentences.zh: 因掊地為穴，度可容其面，俯窺焉而卒，稾葬於道側。

translations.literal: He then beat the ground into a pit, estimated it could hold his face, looked down into it, and died. He was buried in straw beside the road.
translations.idiomatic: He beat the ground into a pit, estimated it could hold his face, looked down into it, and died. He was buried in straw beside the road.

sentences.zh: 後累月，故人取其屍將改葬之，其體甚輕，空空然若蟬蛻焉。

translations.literal: Months later an old friend took his corpse to rebury it; the body was very light, empty as if a cicada's slough.
translations.idiomatic: Months later an old friend took his corpse to rebury it; the body was very light, empty as a cicada's slough.

sentences.zh: 所定《古今尚書》並《釋文》並行於世。

translations.literal: His collated 《Ancient and Modern Documents》 and 《Commentary》 both circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collated 《Ancient and Modern Documents》 and 《Commentary》 both circulated in the world.
